2c876dc2c4177a81: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved RM2.5 million to upgrade the newly renamed UiTM Tun Arshad Ayub Jalan Othman campus in Petaling Jaya.
The allocation was announced by Anwar during the Himpunan Mesra Alumni UiTM here, following his declaration that the UiTM Jalan Othman campus would be renamed UiTM Tun Arshad Ayub Jalan Othman.
The campus traces its origins to Dewan Latihan RIDA, established in 1956, and is closely associated with the beginnings of UiTM.
Anwar said the allocation was part of the government's efforts to strengthen UiTM and ensure its institutions continued to provide quality educational opportunities for Bumiputera students.
He also reaffirmed the government's commitment to the Bumiputera development agenda, particularly in education, economic growth and social development.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said UiTM's operating and development allocation had increased significantly under the Madani government.
He said UiTM received RM3.08 billion in 2026, compared with less than RM2 billion before the Madani government took office.
Anwar also stressed the need for funds allocated to Malay and Bumiputera agencies to be properly managed and protected from abuse and misappropriation.
He said strengthening UiTM's capabilities was important to ensure the university continued to progress as a centre of academic excellence.

The prime minister also announced RM100,000 each for the TUNaS Belia NEET programme and the Himpunan Mesra Alumni UiTM as a show of support and appreciation for the efforts of the UiTM Malaysia Alumni Federation (PAUiTM).
9e7f09357da38116: KUALA LUMPUR: S. Sivasangari is one match away from defending her Asian Games gold medal and earning a spot at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics after advancing to the women's final in Nagoya today.
The world No. 5 defeated Hong Kong's world No. 21 Chan Sin Yuk 11-6, 11-8, 11-7 in the semi-finals.
She will face India's world No. 17 Anahat Singh, the reigning world junior champion, in tomorrow's final.
Anahat reached the final after stunning world No. 6 Satomi Watanabe of Japan 9-11, 11-13, 12-10, 11-6, 11-3.
10236c4603871aec: JAKARTA: Harimau Malaya did not travel to Jakarta to buckle under the hosts' pressure, says naturalised forward Bergson da Silva ahead of meeting with Indonesia at Gelora Bung Karno (GBK) on Monday.
Instead, the 35-year-old believes Harimau Malaya's claws cut deep when the squad unites and pools their collective strength against tough opposition.

Bergson spoke with confidence after enjoying a dream debut for Malaysia, finding the net in Harimau Malaya's 3-0 win over Bangladesh in their opening FIFA Asean Cup Division 1 Group A fixture at the GBK on Friday.
"Every match is going to be tough, as I've said before. We know Indonesia's strength and that they are playing on home soil in this competition.
"But as Malaysians, we need to stay focused on capitalising on every opportunity against them," he said.
Bergson, who netted Malaysia's third goal in the 52nd minute off a La'Vere Corbin-Ong assist, admitted that taking on Indonesia will demand a whole new level of motivation compared to the opener.
However, he believes Harimau Malaya can take the fight to their rivals if every player puts the team ahead of personal glory.
"I think the motivation is different. If we combine all our strengths, we can achieve what we want, and that is our mentality.
"We are not afraid of anyone and will keep pushing forward to achieve what we want. That is why we came to Jakarta, and that's to play in matches like this," he said.

The 3-0 win over Bangladesh handed Malaysia a flawless start, while Indonesia also kicked off their campaign with a 2-0 victory over Singapore, setting the stage for a high-stakes duel between two sides tied on three points.
cb0e657b73ab2019: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas across the country, except Sarawak, until 5pm today.
In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the adverse weather was expected to affect the whole of Perlis and Penang.

In Kedah, the affected areas are Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Yan, Kuala Muda, Baling, Kulim and Bandar Baharu, while in Perak, they comprise Kerian, Larut, Matang and Selama, Kuala Kangsar, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Bagan Datuk and Hilir Perak.
The warning also covers Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang, Pasir Puteh and Kuala Krai in Kelantan, as well as Besut, Hulu Terengganu and Dungun in Terengganu.
In Pahang, the areas involved are Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub and Bentong, while in Selangor, the warning covers Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor and Klang.
In Negeri Sembilan, the affected areas are Seremban, Port Dickson, Rembau and Kuala Pilah, while in Johor, they are Tangkak, Muar, Batu Pahat and Mersing.

In Sabah, the warning covers Sandakan (Kinabatangan, Paitan and Sandakan), Tawau (Lahad Datu and Kunak), the West Coast, Interior (Membakut, Tambunan, Keningau, Sipitang, Beaufort and Tenom) and Kudat (Kota Marudu). — Bernama
d367ecc4590a22d5: JAKARTA: Wildfires that tore through Indonesian Borneo's vast tropical forests have piled pressure on critically endangered Bornean orangutans, the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) said Saturday.
Indonesia has been battling fires for weeks in parts of Borneo and Sumatra, sending suffocating haze across the islands and neighbouring Malaysia and Singapore.
Fires are currently burning within habitats containing 52 per cent of Borneo's orangutan population, including 13 of the 20 largest remaining populations, it said.
"Fire and smoke exposure impose measurable physiological, behavioural and ecological costs on orangutans in peat forest habitats," the conservation network said.
During haze, orangutans show signs of fat breakdown despite eating more and resting more, suggesting elevated energy demands likely from an immune system forced to work harder, it said.
Wildfires have also been reported in the habitats of five gibbon species across Sumatra and Borneo, the conservation network said.

"Gibbons breathe the same smoke-laden air as the people living alongside them, and there is every reason to expect they suffer similar respiratory harm, on top of habitat loss and disruption to the behaviours that keep wild populations viable."
As of Tuesday, Indonesia had rescued 100 animals, including 53 orangutans, that were threatened by the blazes, a forestry ministry spokesman said.
Conservationists call on the authorities to go beyond first response and implement prevention measures.
"Emergency response must be followed by sustained investment in preventing future fires," Ronna Saab of Forum Konservasi Orangutan Indonesia (FORINA) said in a statement.

Those measures include "protecting and rewetting peatlands, addressing drainage and deforestation, and ensuring burned forests are protected from subsequent conversion and appropriately restored," Ronna said.
The Indonesian government said more than 202,000 hectares of land were burnt countrywide between January and July, the latest available data.
The Nusantara Atlas project has put the number at closer to 900,000 hectares between January and August.--AFP
79322a56b7606dc9: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 26 — The Defence Ministry (Mindef) today launched the National Defence Literacy Programme to boost the public’s awareness, knowledge and understanding of national defence, security and sovereignty.

Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said a shifting security threat landscape demands a deeper understanding of national defence, and a recognition of the role Malaysians can play in safeguarding the nation’s sovereignty.

“This is where what we call defence literacy comes in. It is an awareness, a body of knowledge and a skill that every citizen must possess,” he told reporters after launching the National Defence Literacy Programme at the Sabah International Convention Centre here today.
Also present were Defence Ministry secretary-general Datuk Lokman Hakim Ali and Army chief Jen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.

Others in attendance were MiDAS chief executive Laksdya Datuk Yusne Mokhtar, Office of Home Affairs and Research secretary Datuk Awang Shaminan Awang Ashaari, and Sabah National Security Council director Datuk Yahya Sulaiman.

Mohamed Khaled said the public must grasp the fact that security threats today are far more complex. They are no longer confined to physical or military danger, but are alive in the digital space too.
“That is exactly why we are running this Literacy Programme. We want to build the people’s resilience. When the people are resilient, it becomes a deterrent force,” he said.

He said defence literacy efforts must be sustained, so the public not only understands defence and security issues better, but also sees the role they can play in contributing to national defence. Sabah was picked as the first state to roll out the programme, before it is expanded nationwide.

Earlier in his speech, Mohamed Khaled framed national defence through three key components: defence as the nation’s fence or shield, defence as the nation’s umbrella, and defence as the anchor or pillar of a sovereign nation.
He said the defence literacy agenda is about showing the public that there are many ways to strengthen the people’s resilience.
“Ways that don’t require anyone to become a soldier or take up arms,” he said, adding that a range of awareness programmes on defence issues will be rolled out actively.
“We want the public to understand one thing clearly: defence issues no longer start with an enemy at our borders or waters. Threats to sovereignty are everywhere,” he said.

The one-day programme featured two headline segments: Bicara Ancaman Kognitif (Talk on Cognitive Threats) and Bicara Pahlawan Negara (Talk on National Warriors). They zeroed in on how threats now target public thought and perception in today’s security landscape.

The Bicara Pahlawan Negara session brought together Major General (Rtd) Datuk Dr Radzi Abd Hamid as moderator and four special panellists: Lieutenant General (Rtd) Datuk Seri Zain Mohd Said SP, Major General Datuk Mohd Halim Khalid PGB, Warrant Officer 1 (Rtd) Freaddey Yojod and Lance Corporal (Rtd) Abdul Rahman Maidin.
The National Defence Literacy Programme is a Mindef initiative led by the Malaysian Institute of Defence and Security (MiDAS) in collaboration with Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia.
At its core, it aims to sharpen public awareness of one simple truth: every layer of society has a role in defending the nation’s security and sovereignty. — Bernama
e1bad34084fe5a12: PETALING JAYA: Putrajaya must first work out the one-third formula for Sabah and Sarawak representation in the Dewan Rakyat before adding any parliamentary seats.

Women, family and community development minister Nancy Shukri said she and several Sarawak leaders, including in the Cabinet, had raised the issue, but the focus had previously been more on state assembly seats.
She said she would support works minister Alexander Nanta Linggi in the Cabinet on the matter of parliamentary seats for Sarawak, Bernama reported.

"How that one-third formula is to be created needs to be discussed together, in terms of legislation," she said after attending an educational guidance programme and Sarawak UiTM’s academic exhibition at SMK Bako in Kuching today.

Nancy, who is also vice-president of the Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu women's movement, said further discussions to determine a suitable method must be held by the Sarawak premier and Sabah chief minister with the federal government.

Previously, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said the government had agreed in principle to increase the ratio of Sabah and Sarawak representation in the Dewan Rakyat, in line with the region’s position in the formation of Malaysia through the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
He said the decision was among the key matters agreed upon at the MA63 implementation action council meeting.
e01d2d7e071bfe88: ATHENS: A body was pulled from the rubble of a collapsed building on Saturday following an explosion in Athens' historic Plaka district, the Greek press agency ANA reported, as rescuers searched for the missing.
The victim is believed to be an American tourist who was staying in a holiday rental with her husband and another couple in an apartment located on the first floor, ANA reported.
Six people were declared missing following the Friday morning explosion, which the city's mayor Haris Doukas attributed to a gas leak.
The building was located just below the Acropolis on a small street that shook the area.
Local press said the missing included a Briton and a Greek woman who lived on the second floor, and four American tourists who were staying on the first floor.
Thirty firefighters have been deployed to the scene with six vehicles, including two specialised rescue vehicles, as well as three search and rescue dogs, according to ANA.
Excavators are clearing the rubble and thermal cameras have been deployed at the scene by rescuers, according to images from AFP.
"The damage extends along the entire street as well as the street behind the building," Doukas explained. "We are talking about an incredible disaster."--AFP
c322a1ff4a346cab: KUALA LUMPUR: With her wedding approaching, singer-actress Bella Astillah has met former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his wife, Tun Dr Hasmah Mohamad Ali, to ask for marriage advice.
Bella, 32, said she was eager to learn how the couple had stayed together for more than 70 years and what helped them navigate life's challenges.
"Today, I received something truly special. My fiancé, Syed Saddiq, and I had the chance to meet Tun M and Tun Hasmah," she shared on Threads.
"One of the things I wanted to ask most was how a marriage can stay strong after more than 70 years together," she added.
Bella said she was deeply moved seeing Mahathir and Hasmah sitting side by side after decades together.
She noted that while people often talk about falling in love, far less is said about how to keep loving the same person as life changes.
"We rarely talk about how to keep loving the same person as the years go by—as we grow older, face hardships, and the world changes around us," she said.
She added that a lasting marriage takes patience, compromise, forgiveness, and understanding.

"More than 70 years—imagine how much joy and hardship they've shared. How much patience, compromise, and forgiveness it takes to reach a point where the person beside you is still the one you chose all those years ago," Bella wrote.
Bella also shared her wish to grow old with Syed Saddiq.
"I looked at Syed and prayed in my heart that one day, when our hair turns grey, and our steps slow down, the person sitting beside me will still be him."
She concluded that love is not about finding a perfect relationship, but about two people choosing each other every day through life's ups and downs.
Bella and Syed Saddiq previously confirmed that they would be tying the knot on Oct 10.
c00fb1248845d7f9: BAGHDAD: The Iraqi government said Saturday it was holding talks with the US to secure an exemption from the ban on Iranian airlines, which has disrupted travel for patients, students and pilgrims.
All Iraqi airports enforced the ban this week, resulting in major disruption at the airport of the holy city of Najaf, the main destination for Iranian flights to Iraq.
"The Iraqi government is holding direct talks with the American side to exempt certain Iraqi airports from these measures," the prime minister's media office said.
An exemption would allow flights to resume "for humanitarian reasons, including medical treatment, education, religious visits, and for the interest of civilians," it added.
Iranian airlines mainly carry Iraqi Shia pilgrims to Iran's holy cities or Iranians visiting sacred sites in Iraq.
The flights also serve Iraqi students studying in Iran and patients seeking medical treatment there.

Several Iraqis told AFP that enforcing the US sanctions has left them scrambling for solutions, with some fearing they would lose access to treatment in Iran or others stranded there with little choice but to take the more than 12-hour journey home by land.
Iraq has joined several countries, including the UAE in enforcing the US ban, after treasury secretary Scott Bessent said Iranian airlines would be "shut down" on Wednesday.
Relations between Iraq and neighbouring Iran, both Shia-majority countries, have long been close, due to religious kinship as well as political and economic interests.
Iraqi airlines stopped flying to Iran at the start of the Middle East war in February.
1218e282cfd87214: SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced that Universiti Teknologi MARA’s (UiTM) Jalan Othman Campus in Petaling Jaya has been renamed UiTM Tun Arshad Ayub Jalan Othman Campus in recognition of the late educationist’s contributions to the development of the institution.

Anwar said the renaming was a tribute to Arshad’s legacy, having played a key role in the development of the Institut Teknologi MARA (ITM) into UiTM, while also being known for his firm emphasis on educational quality, good governance and expanding educational opportunities for Bumiputera students.
He described Arshad as a highly respected Malay educationist who was firm and uncompromising, particularly when it came to education, quality and opportunities for Malay students.

Anwar said Arshad had also maintained a strong commitment to governance and institutional integrity, rather than using Malay institutions or agencies for personal gain or allowing them to be undermined by misconduct.

“Today’s younger generation may not remember him, but as times change, many have emerged claiming to be champions of the Malay cause and speaking about the struggle for the Malays. However, not many have maintained the same commitment to good governance or refrained from using Malay institutions and agencies to enrich themselves or undermine them,” he said.

Anwar said Arshad’s legacy should therefore be viewed not only in terms of his role in establishing and strengthening the institution, but also in the way he managed it and upheld good governance, which he said contributed to the growth of ITM’s Jalan Othman campus.
He was speaking at the UiTM Alumni Gathering with the Prime Minister at the university’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor (DATC) here today. — Bernama
e375ade6b90c86d2: AICHI: Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah are just one step away from guaranteeing at least a bronze medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after booking their spot in the quarter-finals today.

The world No. 5 faced little trouble, needing just 29 minutes to defeat Thailand's Napapakorn Tungkasatan-Hathaithip Mijad 21-8, 21-12 in their second-round clash at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium.
Pearly-Thinaah will face either Japan's Yuki Fukushima-Mayu Matsumoto or India's Gayatri Gopichand-Treesa Jolly for a spot in the semi-finals.
Advancing to the semi-finals would guarantee Pearly-Thinaah at least a bronze medal for Malaysia.
The last time Malaysia secured a medal in the Asian Games women's doubles event was through Vivian Hoo-Woon Khe Wei, who won bronze at the 2014 Incheon edition.
At the 2022 Hangzhou Asian Games, Pearly-Thinaah crashed out in the quarter-finals.
303ed122de220c58: PADANG BESAR: Kementerian Komunikasi menerusi Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (SKMM) akan membantu Kementerian Kesihatan (KKM) membuat penghantaran ubat melalui pos secara percuma, kepada pesakit yang memohon perkhidmatan itu mulai 1 Okt ini.
Menteri Komunikasi, Fahmi Fadzil, berkata inisiatif itu, akan dilaksanakan di seluruh negara melalui peruntukan dana kira-kira RM5 juta.

“Sebelum ini pesakit perlu membayar untuk penghantaran ubat melalui pos tetapi mulai 1 Okt ini, semua yang terlibat tidak lagi perlu membayar dan ditanggung sepenuhnya oleh kerajaan melalui SKMM,” katanya.
Beliau berkata demikian kepada pemberita selepas meninjau projek inisiatif Pemacu Ekosistem dan Ketersambungan Kesihatan Digital Negara (Persada), di Klinik Kesihatan Padang Besar di sini hari ini.
Turut hadir Ketua Setiausaha Kementerian Komunikasi Abdul Halim Hamzah dan Pengarah Kesihatan Perlis Dr Ghazali Chik.

Pada Jun lepas, Fahmi dilaporkan berkata kerajaan akan menanggung sepenuhnya kos penghantaran ubat kepada kira-kira 80,000 pesakit sebulan, menerusi Program Ubat Melalui Pos (UMP) hasil kerjasama SKMM dan KKM.
2565193c206d2ffa: SUBANG JAYA, Sept 26 — The removal of the 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement for private education institutions (IPS) will not undermine the government’s agenda to empower the community, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today.
He said implementation and follow-up measures arising from the removal of the requirement would be handled by the relevant ministries according to their respective jurisdictions.
Akmal Nasrullah said the Bumiputera empowerment agenda should instead be viewed in terms of strengthening the community’s capacity to participate in and expand its presence in the economy.

“The government will continue to strengthen the Bumiputera empowerment agenda through approaches that can increase their capacity to continue growing and participating in economic activities,” he said.
He was speaking to reporters after attending the closing ceremony of the Rehda Institute Youth Initiative (RIYI) 2026 here.

Akmal Nasrullah said the government remained focused on increasing Bumiputera participation and capabilities in economic activities, and that removing the equity requirement did not signal any reduction in its commitment to the community’s economic empowerment.

At the event, the minister was also presented with the RIYI 2026 closing summary report, which highlighted a gap between students’ expectations and employers’ assessments of graduates’ workplace readiness.

The survey found that 41.6 per cent of student respondents considered one to three months a realistic period for fresh graduates to begin adding commercial value at work, compared with just 2.9 per cent of employers who held the same view.

Meanwhile, 62 per cent of students said they felt adequately prepared by their universities, while only 32.3 per cent of employers agreed that local universities sufficiently prepared graduates for workplace realities.

The survey involved students and recent graduates from 21 Malaysian universities as well as employers, although the report cautioned that the findings came from targeted surveys and were not nationally representative.

The report also highlighted the growing impact of artificial intelligence on entry-level employment. Some 76.4 per cent of student respondents said they regularly used AI tools, while half of the employers surveyed expected AI to reduce the number of entry-level positions they would hire for over the next three years.

On career development, 79.4 per cent of employers said they were willing to provide structured training and a clear career path in return for a commitment from employees to stay, while 67.6 per cent of students said they would accept such an arrangement.

The survey also found that 82.4 per cent of students and 58.3 per cent of employers supported compulsory salary-range disclosure in job advertisements, while 57.1 per cent of students said they were likely or very likely to work outside Malaysia within five years.

The findings form part of RIYI 2026’s focus on narrowing the gap between universities and industry, with the initiative bringing students together with industry leaders to gain exposure to workplace expectations, career development and the skills needed in a technology-driven economy.
Rehda Institute chairman Datuk Jeffrey Ng Tiong Lip said closer collaboration between universities and industry was needed to give students earlier exposure to workplace realities.
“A university qualification provides an important foundation, but young people also need to understand how workplaces operate, how decisions are made and what employers expect from them.

“This is where RIYI plays an important role in bringing students closer to industry through direct engagement and mentorship, while helping them develop the judgement, resilience, communication and adaptability needed to build sustainable careers,” he said.

The RIYI 2026 programme brought together students from more than 21 universities, with its final session focusing on AI’s impact on junior roles, productivity, decision-making and the capabilities expected of future leaders.
62b2275b0fa78bf0: PETALING JAYA: Barisan Nasional (BN) akan mengadakan dua perjumpaan berasingan dengan dua kumpulan berbeza minggu depan bagi membincangkan kerjasama politik menjelang PRN Melaka.

Pengerusinya, Zahid Hamidi, berkata dua pertemuan itu diatur ibu pejabat BN pada tarikh dan waktu berbeza, tanpa mendedahkan identiti dua kumpulan terbabit, sama ada Perikatan Nasional (PN), Pakatan Harapan atau parti lain.

"Baru nak bincang, nak dedah macam mana? Bincang dululah. Kita bagi pada (Pengerusi BN Melaka) Ab Rauf (Yusoh) maklum," katanya menurut Sinar Harian pada Program Musyawarah Nasional: Membongkar Polemik Tanah Melayu di MITC, Ayer Keroh.
Ditanya kumpulan mana paling hampir menjalin kerjasama dengan BN, beliau berkata, ia akan diperhalusi.

"Kita mesti melihat dari segi mudarat dan munasabah, mana yang lebih. Sudah tentu kita sebagai sebuah gabungan politik atas nama BN mahu melihat dari jangka sederhana dan panjang dari segi manfaat kepada negara dan khususnya kepada gabungan parti kita yang ada.”
Ditanya jika BN akan berunding dengan PAS kerana PN kini digantung Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan, jelasnya, perkara itu diserahkan kepada kepimpinan PN dan setiausaha agungnya.
"Saya serahkan perkara itu kepada setiausaha agung dan pengerusi PN untuk menentukan, tapi kami lebih selesa jika dalam sesebuah parti daripada gabungan yang telah terburai itu."
bf61577e51d21d44: KUALA LUMPUR: National coach Brendon Carolan believes Malaysia are ready to beat China to remain unbeaten in the Asian Games hockey competition after edging Pakistan 5-4.
World No. 15 Malaysia fought back with two goals in the last four minutes to beat world No. 12 Pakistan in a Group B match in Gifu, virtually qualifying for the semi-finals.
The Speedy Tigers, who have 12 points from four matches, take on China on Monday.
Carolan said: "I am really proud of the guys as they were mentally resilient to come back to get a result.
"However, the third quarter wasn't our best again. It was disappointing to allow a team to score that many penalty corners. After we have done so much work, it was not great for us.
"Now we focus on China. We must beat them to top the group.
"We need to prepare well for our final game. We respect China, and we will not underestimate them," he said.
Pakistan took the lead in the third minute via a penalty corner, but Malaysia fought back to take a 2-1 lead through Shello Silverius in the fifth minute and Faizal Saari in the 23rd minute.
Sufyan responded with goals in the 39th and 43rd minutes off penalty corners to give Pakistan a 3-2 lead.
Fitri Saari levelled for Malaysia in the 45th minute, before Sufyan restored Pakistan's lead a minute later.
Malaysia continued to press and equalised through Shello in the 56th minute.
Azrai Aizad Abu Kamal scored the winner three minutes from time to seal victory over the former world champions.
The tournament champions will qualify for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
Malaysia's best Asian Games results were silver medals at the 2010 Guangzhou and 2018 Jakarta-Palembang editions.
1c5e29a737d837a4: KUCHING, Sept 26 — Sarawak will establish an authority to oversee, manage and develop the state’s lake areas in a comprehensive manner.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said the initiative is part of the state’s development plans for the next five years.
He said the plans took into account approaches adopted by other states to develop lake areas as resort destinations while providing better facilities.
“Insya-Allah, we will establish an authority to oversee all our lakes in Sarawak, including rivers with potential,” he said at the launch of the Sarawakku Sayang 2026 programme in Betong today.
Abang Johari said the initiative was also expected to add value to the state’s economic growth while further strengthening Sarawak’s existing strengths.

Meanwhile, he said the Centre for Technology Excellence Sarawak (CENTEXS) would establish a Flying School Academy in Betong to support the state’s efforts to advance modern agriculture through drone technology.
“Drones are important, in addition to aircraft, which is why I support the establishment of a flying academy here in collaboration with the private sector.
“This is because licences are required, while the open airspace here provides a conducive environment for students to learn how to operate drones in the Betong area,” he said. — Bernama
193bc0c09dcab0f6: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today he is waiting for Transport Minister Anthony Loke's resignation letter.
"Wait for the letter," he said briefly when met by reporters after the Himpunan Mesra Alumni Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) at the Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor (DATC), UiTM, here.

Loke announced his decision to resign as Transport Minister following the DAP Central Executive Committee (CEC) meeting on Sept 19, citing the issue surrounding the conditional pardon involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
He said other DAP ministers and deputy ministers would remain in the Federal Government.
Anwar had previously said he had advised Loke to reconsider his decision and would hold further discussions with the DAP secretary-general to hear his official explanation.
Anwar also said DAP should not bow to pressure from parties with political interests to withdraw from the unity government simply because they wanted to see the administration become unstable.
He said he respected Loke and DAP's longstanding principles of opposing kleptocracy and corruption, which had made it difficult for the party to deal with the Pardons Board's decision.
Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, has maintained that he would resign from the Cabinet and said he would submit his resignation letter after returning to Malaysia from China.

The Federal Territories Pardons Board granted Najib a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, subject to conditions including payment of a RM50 million fine.
f1dc5728e82ae0c7: JAKARTA: Interim Harimau Malaya head coach Tan Cheng Hoe has 48 hours to rejuvenate his squad, address tactical shortcomings and devise a winning formula ahead of facing hosts Indonesia on Monday.
A convincing 3-0 win over Bangladesh in their opening Group A fixture at the Gelora Bung Karno (GBK) provided the ideal start.
Cheng Hoe, however, is adamant that complacency must not creep in.
Instead, the tight turnaround is dedicated to ensuring Malaysia is fully prepared for an Indonesian side that also won their opener.
"My focus is on bringing the players to an optimal state of readiness and recovery. At the same time, the medical team needs to assess who is available and who isn't," Cheng Hoe said.
Beyond physical recovery, the coaching staff is dissecting their opener while formulating tactical plans for Indonesia.
Despite the comfortable scoreline, Cheng Hoe acknowledged areas needing improvement, particularly ball retention and transitions.

"We need to analyse how we played against Bangladesh and, at the same time, break down Indonesia's game. We are ready to compete," he added, crediting new additions Bergson da Silva, Manuel Hidalgo and Brad Tapp for providing vital energy, depth and confidence to the squad.
That self-belief was echoed by naturalised forward Hidalgo, who insisted Malaysia will not feel intimidated by Indonesia's formidable reputation or their vocal home support.
"Indonesia are a very strong team. Nobody can deny that, but so is Malaysia. So I believe in our chances," said the 30-year-old, who played a key role against Bangladesh.
Having plied his trade in Malaysia for years, Hidalgo believes squad chemistry is already thriving.

"I know the quality they have. They are fantastic players. It's always about team bonding, and I feel the best is yet to come," he said, adding that representing the country was an emotional milestone.
"Malaysia has given me everything, so being able to give back is amazing. I'm exhausted, but very happy."
The opening win was equally memorable for fellow debutant Bergson da Silva.
Having arrived in Malaysia in 2021 with Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT), the Brazilian striker cleared his five-year residency and received FIFA eligibility on September 13.
He marked his international debut by scoring Malaysia's third goal against Bangladesh.
Off the pitch, the 35-year-old Bergson has embraced local life so deeply that fans have affectionately nicknamed him "Ahmad Bergson."
"Truly Ahmad Bergson now, right?" he joked.
"I feel like a Malaysian. I am so touched by the love they have shown me, and I want to repay it on the pitch."

a4b261ba9c6ed6f5: PADANG BESAR: Pelaksanaan projek rintis sistem pengurusan Rekod Perubatan Elektronik (EMR) menerusi inisiatif Pemacu Ekosistem dan Ketersambungan Kesihatan Digital Negara (PERSADA) di fasiliti kesihatan di Perlis, memberikan impak positif dari segi masa menunggu pesakit.

Menteri Komunikasi Fahmi Fadzil berkata projek di negeri itu sejak empat bulan lepas menunjukkan, lebih 86% pesakit dapat bertemu dengan doktor dalam tempoh kurang 60 minit manakala 62.8% pesakit boleh berbuat demikian kurang 30 minit.
“Ia berjaya memanfaatkan lebih 200,000 pesakit di Perlis.
"Saya juga menerima beberapa maklum balas tentang sistem dan menyampaikan beberapa cadangan, untuk memastikan sistem ini selamat digunakan, mudah untuk para pekerja Kementerian Kesihatan,” katanya.

Beliau bercakap kepada pemberita selepas meninjau projek PERSADA di Klinik Kesihatan Padang Besar di sini hari ini, yang turut disertai Ketua Setiausaha Kementerian Komunikasi Abdul Halim Hamzah dan Pengarah Kesihatan Perlis Dr Ghazali Chik.

Fahmi berkata menerusi projek itu, doktor tidak perlu lagi menunggu kad sejarah kesihatan pesakit secara manual, dengan kesemua maklumat berkaitan telah tersedia dalam bentuk yang lebih mudah untuk semakan doktor menerusi sistem berkenaan.

“Saya lihat sendiri memang doktor-doktor memaklumkan ini memudahkan kerja mereka dan mengurangkan masa untuk menunggu rekod datang kepada mereka, disimpan dalam cloud based data, yang lebih selamat,” katanya.

Sehubungan dengan itu, Fahmi berkata kementeriannya berhasrat untuk memperluas penggunaan sistem itu untuk manfaat negeri lain, namun akan meneliti beberapa aspek terlebih dahulu termasuk kemudahan Internet, bagi memastikan sistem itu dapat digunakan dengan lebih cekap dan berkesan.

“Saya lihat ia dapat dimanfaatkan di negeri lain, kita akan meneliti beberapa aspek, kerana isu dihadapi mungkin sesetengah negeri, ada klinik kesihatan Internet belum lagi pantas, saya dimaklumkan keperluan Internet untuk sistem ini sekurang-kurangnya 100mbps,” katanya.

Dalam pada itu, Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (SKMM) dalam kenyataan memaklumkan melalui PERSADA, ketersambungan yang diperkukuh akan menyokong perkongsian maklumat kesihatan lebih lancar serta menjadi asas kepada pelaksanaan aspirasi “Satu Individu, Satu Rekod Kesihatan”.

“Rekod kesihatan pesakit dapat menyokong kesinambungan rawatan apabila mendapatkan perkhidmatan di fasiliti atau lokasi yang berbeza, sekali gus mewujudkan pengalaman rawatan yang lebih lancar dan teratur, serta membantu mengurangkan tempoh menunggu,” menurutnya.

Menurut kenyataan itu, kerjasama rentas kementerian antara Kementerian Komunikasi melalui SKMM dengan Kementerian Kesihatan (KKM), dapat memperkukuh penyampaian perkhidmatan serta ketersambungan digital dan teknologi yang lebih bersepadu.

Sementara itu, Fahmi berkata SKMM mengintegrasikan perkhidmatan telekesihatan melalui 17 Pusat Sebaran Maklumat Nasional (NADI) di Perlis, yang membolehkan penduduk setempat mendapatkan perkhidmatan tertentu termasuk saringan kesihatan di pusat NADI, tanpa perlu ke klinik kesihatan.

“Kita akan memperlihatkan kerjasama lebih erat antara NADI di bawah MCMC dan klinik kesihatan serta klinik desa bukan sahaja di Perlis, tetapi seluruh negara untuk memudahkan pesakit mendapatkan rawatan,” katanya.
5aafe21084917f61: BATU KAWAN, Sept 26 — The Ministry of Entrepreneur and Cooperatives Development (Kuskop) has channelled nearly RM10 billion through various support and financing programmes under the ‘Power Up 10K’ initiative to about 270,000 entrepreneurs nationwide as of the end of August.

Its minister Steven Sim Chee Keong said the achievement was among the reasons Kuskop had proposed to the Ministry of Finance (MOF) for larger allocations for the micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and cooperative sectors under Budget 2027.

“The RM10 billion is part of the RM15 billion target to be channelled to the MSME and cooperative sectors this year. In Penang alone, RM760 million was channelled in the first eight months, benefiting about 6,000 entrepreneurs.

“If Malaysians want to do business in Malaysia but do not have opportunities, let us not talk about overseas markets first. We must ensure Malaysian businesses, products and services can penetrate the domestic market before going abroad,” he told reporters after the 2026 “Hebatkan Perniagaan Malaysia” (HPM) Carnival, Penang edition, at Batu Kawan Stadium here today.
Sim noted that financing support for the MSME sector had been increased to RM60 billion this year from RM50 billion previously.

He said Kuskop had also proposed reducing the cost of doing business and improving government delivery efficiency to help MSMEs expand. Measures included simplifying government processes, shortening processing times and reducing related fees and charges.

“If we cannot control global oil prices, at least we can control local costs. Government processes must be made easier and processing times, fees and charges, including taxes where possible, should be reduced so that MSMEs can have some breathing space,” he said.

Sim advised that delays in obtaining licences, permits or financing could cause entrepreneurs to lose business opportunities. He added that Kuskop, through Tekun Nasional, had reduced the financing application period to seven days from 30 to 40 days previously, while financing below RM20,000 must be approved within 24 hours.

“The principles Kuskop has conveyed to MOF are, firstly, more funding for the MSME and cooperative sectors; secondly, a lower cost of doing business; and thirdly, greater government delivery efficiency,” he said. — Bernama
72aefc9d1928ebdc: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has yet to receive DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook's letter of resignation as transport minister.
Anwar sidestepped queries from reporters on Loke's status as a Cabinet minister, simply saying he was "waiting for the (resignation) letter" from the DAP leader.
Anwar, the Pakatan Harapan chairman, previously urged Loke to reconsider his decision to resign from the Cabinet over former prime minister Najib Razak's conditional pardon.
The PKR president said DAP should not succumb to pressure from those who want the party to withdraw from the government simply to destabilise the administration.
Anwar had said he would further discuss the matter with Loke to hear his official explanation.
The DAP secretary-general has nonetheless stood firm on his resignation, saying he would submit his resignation letter upon returning from a working visit to China.
According to a transport ministry invitation, Loke is scheduled to officiate the Maritime Week 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre on Tuesday.
Anwar also sidestepped questions on Perikatan Nasional's suspension by the Registrar of Societies, directing reporters to ask home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail about the matter instead.
fe7f3109c2cabdc4: PADANG BESAR, Sept 26 — The pilot Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system implemented under the National Digital Health Ecosystem and Connectivity Driver (Persada) initiative at health facilities in Perlis has had a positive impact on patient waiting times, said Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.

The communications minister said the project, which has been implemented in the state for the past four months, showed that more than 86 per cent of patients were able to see a doctor in less than 60 minutes, while 62.8 per cent did so in less than 30 minutes.

“It has benefited more than 200,000 patients in Perlis. I have also received some feedback on the system and made several suggestions to ensure that it is safe to use and easy for Health Ministry staff to operate,” he told reporters after inspecting the Persada project at the Padang Besar Health Clinic here today.
Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and Perlis Health director Dr Ghazali Chik.
Fahmi said doctors no longer had to wait for patients’ medical records to be retrieved manually, as all relevant information could be accessed through the system.
“The doctors said the system made their work easier and reduced the time spent waiting for patients’ medical records to reach them, as they are stored in the cloud, which is more secure,” he said.

Fahmi said the ministry plans to expand the system to other states but would first assess several factors, including internet connectivity, to ensure that it could be used efficiently and effectively.

“I believe it can benefit other states, but we will look at several aspects because some states may face certain challenges. I was informed that the system requires an internet connection of at least 100 Mbps,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in a statement, said that Persada would facilitate smoother sharing of health information and lay the foundation for the implementation of the ‘One Individual, One Health Record’ aspiration.

“Patients’ health records can help ensure continuity of care when they seek treatment at different facilities or locations, providing a smoother and more organised experience while helping to reduce waiting times,” it said.

According to the statement, cross-ministerial cooperation between the Communications Ministry, through MCMC, and the Health Ministry (MOH) would help strengthen service delivery, as well as digital connectivity and the integration of technology.

Fahmi added that MCMC had integrated telehealth services through 17 National Information Dissemination Centres (NADI) in Perlis, enabling local residents to access certain services, including health screenings, at the centres without having to visit a health clinic.

“We will strengthen cooperation between NADI centres under MCMC and health clinics as well as rural clinics, not only in Perlis but nationwide, to make it easier for patients to access treatment,” he said. — Bernama
0936a8f88469baeb: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government remained dissatisfied with wage levels despite rising productivity and high profits recorded by some companies.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said stronger measures to address the issue would be among the government's priorities in the upcoming 2027 Budget.

Anwar said the government had already taken steps to raise wages, including increasing public sector salaries, raising the private-sector minimum wage to RM1,700 and setting a RM3,100 minimum wage for government-linked investment companies (GLICs).
However, he said these measures were not enough to ensure workers benefited fairly from economic growth and rising productivity.

"I am at the final stage of the Budget, and I certainly have to address this issue more seriously," he said during a question-and-answer session at the Himpunan Mesra Alumni Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) at the Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor (DATC), UiTM, here.
Anwar said Malaysia's productivity had continued to increase, but wage growth remained relatively low.
He said this was particularly concerning in large companies, plantations, industries and factories that recorded high profits but continued to offer relatively low wages.
"I am still not satisfied because large companies, plantations, industries and factories that make very high profits still have low wage rates," he said.
Anwar said Malaysia needed to ensure that increases in productivity were reflected in workers' wages.
Citing South Korea as an example, he said productivity and wages there had generally increased alongside each other, although not necessarily at the same rate.
He said the government therefore needed to take a more active role in addressing wage disparities.

"We have to use the government's power to put pressure," he said, while acknowledging that the government also needed to engage employers carefully to avoid companies threatening to shut down operations or relocate to other countries.

Anwar said the government had already raised public sector salaries, with the latest adjustment resulting in increases of between 15 and 30 per cent, with lower-paid workers receiving larger increases.
For GLICs, he said the government had set a RM3,100 minimum wage from last year and was now looking at how the policy could better address the needs of graduates and postgraduates.
"If it is the minimum wage, those who are graduates or have postgraduate qualifications should be given attention," he said.

Anwar said the issue of wages was also closely linked to Malaysia's efforts to move towards a higher-value economy by attracting investments in sectors such as electrical and electronics, artificial intelligence and other specialised fields.
He said universities, including UiTM, needed to work directly with industry to ensure their curricula kept pace with changing skills requirements.
"Sometimes, engineering cannot use a curriculum from five years ago," he said, adding that universities needed to respond to industry demand for specialised engineering and AI-related skills.
Anwar said developing workers with specialised skills would help Malaysia secure higher-value jobs and improve wages.

40bb3fd1d6914eae: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has tasked the UiTM Malaysia Alumni Federation with evaluating major Bumiputera agencies, including UiTM, and recommending ways to strengthen them.
Anwar said between 7 and 10 alumni should be selected for the task, including people who were not necessarily affiliated with the government.
He said the group would be given the opportunity to assess the performance and role of major Bumiputera agencies and identify areas for improvement.

"I want to give a guarantee today to the alumni that, to demonstrate our seriousness, I will provide the opportunity and avenue for you to evaluate every major programme of Bumiputera agencies, including UiTM, so that they can be improved and enhanced," he said in his address at the Himpunan Mesra Alumni UiTM at the Shah Alam campus.
Anwar said the alumni should also advise on academic disciplines and faculties that should be expanded to meet the demands of the future economy.
Among the areas he highlighted were artificial intelligence (AI), quantum computing, healthcare and other emerging fields.
"Give your views, give your recommendations, and I guarantee that, God willing, we will give them the attention needed to enhance their capabilities," he said.
Anwar said the initiative would allow alumni to contribute directly to strengthening institutions that had played an important role in expanding educational opportunities for Bumiputera students.
He said the government should draw on the experience of former leaders and others who had seen first-hand the strengths and weaknesses of Bumiputera agencies.
"We need to harness all our strengths.
"There are experienced people from the past who can be utilised to the best of our ability because they have seen the strengths and weaknesses themselves," he said.
Anwar said the aim was to ensure UiTM continued to improve its capabilities and become a leading centre of academic excellence.
He said the university was already regarded as a successful institution but needed to take further steps to strengthen its academic capabilities.
"We want UiTM to continue producing graduates like these, but there must be a stride in its capability to raise its standards," he said.
975ce4316827ad95: KUCHING, Sept 26 — Putrajaya must first work out the one-third formula for Sabah and Sarawak representation in the Dewan Rakyat before adding any parliamentary seats.

Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said she and several Sarawak leaders, including in Cabinet, have raised the issue, but the focus had previously been more on state assembly seats.
“Speaking on voicing out in terms of (Parliamentary) seats, I am with Yang Berhormat Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi in Cabinet.

“How that one-third formula is to be created needs to be discussed together, in terms of legislation,” she said after the Motivation and Guidance Programme for Study Opportunities and UiTM Sarawak Branch Academic Exhibition at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Bako here today.

Nancy, who is also vice-president of the Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) Women’s Movement, said further discussions to determine a suitable method and measure must be held between the Sarawak premier, Sabah chief minister and the Federal Government.

Previously, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government had agreed in principle to increase the ratio of Sabah and Sarawak representation in the Dewan Rakyat, in line with the regions’ position in the formation of Malaysia through the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
He said the decision was among the key matters agreed at the Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council meeting. — Bernama
7809ce187f1c416c: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) to review UiTM Holdings' governance and management over concerns about the company's losses.
Anwar said the review should be conducted in cooperation with the UiTM vice-chancellor and the Prime Minister's Department, which would provide support where necessary.
"Please look into UiTM Holdings and find ways to work together with the vice-chancellor.
"The Prime Minister's Department and my office will provide cooperation and push for this," he said.

Anwar was responding to an audience member who wanted the government and the UiTM Malaysia Alumni Federation to review the management of UiTM Holdings, which the student claimed had recorded losses of more than RM100 million.
The issue was raised during a question-and-answer session at the Himpunan Mesra Alumni UiTM at the Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor, UiTM, here.
Anwar said the review should first identify weaknesses in the management and operations of UiTM Holdings before any action was taken.
He said that financial losses alone should not be treated as evidence of wrongdoing, as companies could experience periods of both profit and loss.
"We do not take action simply because a company makes a loss. We take action if there is fraud, abuse of power or misappropriation," he said.
Anwar said any wrongdoing uncovered through the review would have to be dealt with accordingly.
He also said that governance was particularly important for Bumiputera agencies, which he said should serve as examples of good management and integrity.
"I am stricter with Bumiputera agencies because they should be an example," he said.
Anwar said the government was focusing on strengthening governance across agencies while ensuring institutions entrusted with public resources were managed responsibly.

In 2023, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) was reported to be investigating UiTM Holdings over allegations involving corruption, abuse of power and embezzlement. MACC later said it was conducting a forensic investigation into the company's accounts to determine how the reported losses occurred.

At the time, UiTM Holdings was reported to have recorded accumulated pre-tax losses of RM157.04 million over four years — 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2021. The Higher Education Ministry said the figure was based on the reported accumulated losses for those years and welcomed investigations into the matter.

According to the earlier report, most of the losses were linked to investments in local film production, while losses were also attributed to UiTM Holdings' stake in Intekma Resort and Convention Centre in Section 7, Shah Alam, which had ceased operations.

be4bd612f0c299ee: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will hold separate talks with two different groups next week as it weighs possible political partnerships ahead of the Melaka state election, chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today.
Zahid declined to identify either group, leaving open whether the meetings would involve Perikatan Nasional (PN), Pakatan Harapan (PH) or other parties.
According to Sinar Harian, he said BN headquarters had arranged the meetings for different dates and times.
“Next week, the headquarters has arranged two separate meetings, on different dates and at different times. Two different groups,” he said.
“We have only just started discussions, so how can we disclose anything yet? Let us discuss it first. We will inform [Melaka BN chairman] Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.”
Asked whether BN would hold talks directly with PAS following PN’s suspension by the Registrar of Societies, Zahid said the matter should be decided by PN’s chairman and secretary-general.

“I leave that matter to the secretary-general and the PN chairman to decide, but we would be more comfortable dealing with an individual party rather than a coalition that is no longer intact,” he said.

His remarks come as PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said separately today that the coalition’s suspension had not affected its negotiations with BN, adding that the talks were more than halfway complete.
When asked which potential partner was closest to reaching an agreement with BN, Zahid said no decision had yet been made.
“That will be examined further, and we have to weigh the risks and what is reasonable, and determine which carries greater weight,” he said.
“As a political coalition under the BN banner, we naturally want to look at the medium- and long-term benefits for the country, and particularly for the parties in our coalition.”
Melaka’s 28-seat state assembly was dissolved on September 23, paving the way for the state’s 16th election.
Under the state constitution, polling must be held within 60 days of dissolution, meaning by November 22.
The Election Commission is due to meet on October 7 to set the nomination and polling dates.
4fa7aad3eeca8ef9: SHAH ALAM: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim berkata beliau masih menunggu surat rasmi daripada Setiausaha Agung DAP Loke Siew Fook berhubung keputusannya untuk meletakkan jawatan sebagai menteri pengangkutan.
“Tunggu surat (daripada Loke),” katanya ringkas ketika ditanya mengenai status Loke dalam Jemaah Menteri.
Anwar ditemui media selepas menghadiri Himpunan Mesra Alumni UiTM Bersama perdana menteri di Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM).
Pada 23 Sept, Loke menegaskan beliau kekal dengan keputusan untuk berundur dan akan menyerahkan surat peletakan jawatannya kepada Anwar sekembali ke tanah air daripada lawatan kerja di China.
Keputusan itu dibuat susulan mesyuarat Jawatankuasa Tertinggi Pusat (CEC) DAP pada 19 Sept berhubung pengampunan bersyarat diberikan kepada bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak.
CEC memutuskan hanya Loke akan menawarkan diri meletakkan jawatan, manakala menteri dan timbalan menteri DAP lain kekal dalam kerajaan.
Anwar sebelum ini meminta Loke mempertimbangkan semula keputusannya dan berkata beliau tidak mahu terburu-buru membuat keputusan mengenai perkara itu.
Dalam perkembangan berasingan, Anwar enggan mengulas lanjut mengenai penggantungan Perikatan Nasional (PN) oleh Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan Malaysia (JPPM).

Bagaimanapun, jabatan itu menjelaskan tindakan berkenaan bukan pembatalan pendaftaran PN dan gabungan itu diberi tempoh munasabah untuk menjawab notis dikeluarkan.
f8b522510cc07ec5: KUALA LUMPUR: Physical bullying accounts for the highest number of complaints received by the Anti-Bullying Tribunal (TAB), with 41 of 56 cases recorded as of yesterday.
TAB president Nurul Husna Awang said the cases involved harmful physical acts such as hitting, pushing, kicking or damaging property.

She said during the same period, TAB also received six complaints involving emotional and psychological bullying, including threats, insults or actions that caused victims to feel afraid, embarrassed or distressed.
"TAB also received five complaints involving verbal or language bullying, including hurtful remarks, ridicule, threats or name-calling.
"Two complaints involved cyberbullying (verbal and language), while cyberbullying (social) and social bullying recorded one complaint each," she said when contacted.
Nurul Husna said teenagers aged 13 to 17 were the largest group recorded as victims during the period, with 35 cases.
They were followed by children aged 7 to 12 with 18 cases, while the remaining three victims were below 7.
She said 33 of the 56 victims were male.
"By ethnicity, 29 victims were Chinese, 24 were Malay and three were Indian.

"Meanwhile, statistics recorded 86 respondents, comprising 65 males and 21 females. The number of respondents exceeded the number of victims as some cases involved more than one perpetrator," she said.
On case status, Nurul Husna said 12 cases remained active, comprising four at the screening stage, seven at the hearing stage and one pending a further hearing.
She said 44 cases had been resolved, comprising 37 complaints rejected at the screening stage, six cases settled through tribunal hearings and one complaint withdrawn by the complainant.
"The time taken to resolve a complaint at the hearing stage is 60 days from the date the hearing begins," she said.

Last Wednesday, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said was reported as saying that awards issued included apologies to victims, participation in counselling programmes and compensation of RM2,000 in one case.
She said this reflected TAB's approach, which was not solely punishment-oriented but also focused on victim recovery and correcting perpetrators' behaviour.
12fb847acb84b0e8: PETALING JAYA: The 16-year-old arrested over the death of a Form 2 student at a sports school in Kuala Pilah, Negeri Sembilan, has been remanded for six days to assist in the murder probe.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Alzafny Ahmad said the remand order was granted by the Seremban magistrates' court this morning, Berita Harian reported.
"The court has placed him under police remand until Oct 1," he said.
The victim, 14, was found unconscious in the school dormitory before being rushed to Hospital Tuanku Ampuan Najihah, where he was pronounced dead.
The case is being probed for murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code, while the victim's family claimed bullying was involved.
69f46130b84b6a79: TOWNSVILLE: A last minute header from Brazilian substitute Rayan salvaged a 1-1 draw with Australia in a thrilling international friendly in Townsville on Friday.
Rayan headed the ball home in the 95th minute to deny the hosts what would have been only their second win over the South American giants.
It was a fitting result from two evenly-matched teams who gave everything in front of a sell-out crowd in the North Queensland city.
"It was a difficult game," Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti conceded.
"The pitch was not so good to play good football on, but we showed fight until the end.
"I think it was a good test for us."
A superb free kick from Australian youngster Nestory Irankunda had looked enough to give the Socceroos an upset win.

With the two sides locked at 0-0 midway through the second half, Irankunda stepped up and drilled his free kick over the defensive wall into the net, leaving Brazil keeper Hugo Souza rooted to the spot.
But Brazil came out and dominated against an increasingly defensive Australian outfit and were rewarded seconds before full-time.
With both teams looking to rebuild after early exits from this year's World Cup, it was the Socceroos who seized the early advantage.
They dominated possession and territory, attacking with width and finding plenty of space on both sides.
Midfielder Connor Metcalfe went close in just the third minute before an Irankunda bullet forced a good save from Souza.
Brazil weathered the storm and began to get into the game, looking increasingly dangerous through in-form Barcelona striker Raphinha and Chelsea forward Estevao.
Raphinha had a good chance with a header straight to Australian keeper Patrick Beach after 20 minutes before Estevao forced a great save from Beach five minutes later.
The Brazil dominance appeared to have paid off in the 46th minute when Estevao scored, but a VAR review saw the goal ruled out due to an earlier foul on Australian captain Harry Soutar.
The second half saw much of the same, with Brazil controlling the centre and the Socceroos finding space out wide.
The visitors were just edging the match and it seemed only a matter of time before they scored, but they were shocked by Irankunda's superb free kick.
The Socceroos defended furiously and looked to have held out for the win, but a last minute corner saw Rayan's header just too powerful for Beach to hold out. --AFP
cc272c002fc4652e: SINGAPORE, Sept 26 — Mamma Mia Focaccia and its hidden champagne bar The Champagnery have closed less than a year after opening, adding to the string of food and beverage outlets shutting their doors in Singapore amid rising costs.

The Amoy Street sandwich shop opened in October 2025 and quickly drew queues, while The Champagnery, tucked behind a red door inside the deli, opened the following month with champagne, cocktails, DJs and focaccia sandwiches.

“Like many in the industry today, we have found it increasingly difficult to keep afloat amid rising costs, and we’ve made the difficult decision to close our doors,” the team said in a joint Instagram post that announced September 23 as their final day.
The team also said Singapore’s F&B and nightlife scene had “had a tough time of late”, expressing hope that conditions would improve for businesses still operating.

Mamma Mia was run by Spanish chef-owner Houssein Haffian and Italian chef Nico, who have both lived in Singapore for about a decade, with Haffian’s Two S Creatives group also behind Asador and Next Door Spanish Cafe.

The closure comes as Singapore’s F&B operators continue to contend with higher operating costs, including labour and rental expenses, putting pressure on businesses even as consumers remain cautious about spending.
04ba6561946888ed: SEREMBAN: A Form Four student held over the death of a Form Two student in Kuala Pilah has been remanded for six days.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the remand application was made at the Seremban magistrate's court here today.
"Police applied for the remand this morning, and the court granted a six-day remand from today until Oct 1," he said.
Earlier, media reports said a Form Two student at a school in Kuala Pilah had died last night, allegedly after being bullied at the school hostel.
The teenager was reportedly found unconscious at the hostel before being taken to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital here, where he was pronounced dead.
Alzafny was earlier reported as saying that police had brought in a 16-year-old boy to assist in the investigation under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
fc5337a246a1c77a: SHENZHEN: Linda Noskova and Karolina Muchova helped the Czech Republic reach their first Billie Jean King Cup final since 2018 with straight-set victories over Spain in Shenzhen on Friday, keeping the Czechs on course for a 12th title.
World number eight Muchova, this year's Wimbledon runner-up, gave the Czechs a winning start by beating Jessica Bouzas Maneiro 7-5 6-4.

"It's been a while since I played in the Billie Jean King Cup, so bringing the first point to our locker room, while also giving Linda some, let's say, air so she doesn't feel as much pressure to win, is important," Muchova said.
Wimbledon champion Noskova then defeated Cristina Bucsa 7-6(5) 6-2 to give the Czechs an unassailable 2-0 lead and seal the tie.

Noskova broke first to move 4-2 ahead before Bucsa fought back to cut the deficit to 5-4 in a topsy-turvy opening set. The 21-year-old Czech edged the tiebreak and then turned a closely contested second set into a rout, winning the final four games and breaking Bucsa twice after the score was locked at 2-2.
The Czechs are captained by former doubles world number one Barbora Strycova.

"We definitely want to make our captain proud," Noskova said. "As she said, the last time we won it, she was on the team. It would be quite beautiful for all of us to have her part of the team and win it once again, just from a different position.
"But I always love to play for the team no matter what. No matter the circumstances or whether we're playing the finals or the qualifiers, nothing changes for me."
The Czechs will face either two-time defending champions Italy or Ukraine in Sunday's final. --REUTERS
9a8594b553ef5f87: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — The national digital transformation agenda must be implemented inclusively and cannot solely benefit those with access to technology.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the digitalisation process must also ensure that the digitally less literate, elderly, low-income groups and small entrepreneurs can enjoy the same benefits.

“We want technology to be a tool that makes people’s lives easier, rather than adding to their burden. We want digitalisation to open up opportunities, not create a divide,” he said during the Madani Kita Programme at the Damansara Damai Community Hall here today.
Gobind, who is also the Damansara Member of Parliament, said the national digitalisation agenda was not solely about technology, but about people.
He said technology was merely a tool and what was important was how it was used to improve people’s lives.
“This is what we mean by digital for the people. Digital is not just about applications. Digital is not just about artificial intelligence (AI). Digital is not just about data and new technologies.
“Digital is about how all these developments ultimately benefit the people,” he said.
He said the measure of a policy’s success relied not only on how many programmes were implemented, but also on the extent to which the people benefited and experienced changes in their daily lives.

Meanwhile, Gobind said the Madani Kita Programme was a platform organised to bring the government closer to the people through the involvement of various ministries, departments and government agencies in a single location.

He said the programme, implemented by Akademi Kenegaraan Malaysia (AKM), allowed the public to interact directly with government agencies, obtain information on services, understand government initiatives, and convey their views, suggestions and problems. — Bernama
be4cad35e863bfbf: PADANG BESAR: The communications ministry, through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, will help the health ministry provide free postal delivery of medicines to patients who opt for the service from next month.

0e090237f648c257: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Running event organisers in the capital are being told to standardise their routes with Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) to curb disruptions to the city with endless road closures.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said one fix worth considering is to set standard routes based on running distances, and make organisers stick to them.

“Three kilometres — this is the route. Five kilometres — this is the route. Organisers cannot just pick whichever route they fancy,” she told reporters after officiating the Mega Cleaning Programme for Hari Cuci Malaysia at the Batu Muda People’s Housing Programme (PPR) here today.
Hannah said the coordination is crucial because road users need to know in advance which routes are affected so they can plan their journeys.
“This week alone, 30 roads are closed for one run. I cannot accept this. I don’t want the public unable to plan their trips into the city. We need to organise these runs properly,” she said.

Hannah said the move is not aimed at stopping such events, but to ensure they can be held in a more orderly manner without disrupting traffic flow, given that more than a million vehicles enter Kuala Lumpur every day.
She said organisers who need different routes could consider less congested locations, while also making use of existing ones such as those used for the Car Free Day programme.
“Kuala Lumpur is a city that needs to be well organised. I don’t want people wasting hours waiting for roads to reopen,” she said. — Bernama
9081d51c8aead3f0: KUALA LUMPUR: Asian Games debutants Nurqayyum Nazmi Nazim-Yong Rui Jie beat the odds to bag a bronze medal in the men's 3m springboard synchro today.
The 20-year-old pair scored 345.81 points across six dives at the Tokyo Aquatics Centre, retaining the bronze won by Syafiq Puteh-Ooi Tze Liang at Hangzhou 2022.
Tze Liang currently coaches the duo.
China's Wang Zong Yuan-Zheng Jiu Yuan took gold with 465.87 points, while Japan's Senri Ikuma-Haruki Suyama claimed silver with 355.56.
Malaysia Aquatics diving technical director Yeoh Ken Nee said the higher degree of difficulty in competitor dive lists had made other pairs appear stronger contenders on paper.
"Nurqayyum-Rui Jie are making their first appearance at the Asian Games, but they performed consistently throughout the competition," Ken Nee said.

"Based on the start list, other countries appeared to have a stronger chance of winning the bronze medal due to their higher-difficulty dives. However, diving is also about consistency and execution under pressure."
Nurqayyum-Rui Jie stayed focused throughout the contest, completing their dives cleanly to finish third, 9.75 points behind the Japanese silver medallists.
"They stayed focused and executed their dives well until the very end, and that consistency allowed Nurqayyum-Rui Jie to secure the bronze medal in this event," he said.
Earlier, Pandelela Rinong-Nur Eilisha Rania Abrar Raj finished fourth in the women's 10m platform synchro.
a81ecc89055e4b2d: KUALA LUMPUR: Local riders have been warned not to underestimate the challenge awaiting them on Stage Two of the Le Tour de Langkawi (LTdL), with the climb up Gunung Jerai expected to provide an early test.
Former national road cyclist Ng Yong Li said the Category 1 ascent could prove difficult not only for Malaysian riders but also for some of the foreign sprinters in the field.
"If possible, I would like to see the local riders put up a strong challenge and first overcome this early obstacle before thinking about the Genting Highlands climb in Stage Five," said Yong Li.
Yong Li was Malaysia's best-placed rider on the Genting Highlands climb in 2007, 2008, 2009 and 2010.
The former Portugal-based Vitoria-ASC continental team rider said the Gunung Jerai climb bears similarities to the final 10 kilometres of the ascent to Genting Highlands.

"That is based on my own experience of climbing Gunung Jerai, although this is the first time it has been included in the LTdL route," said Yong Li, who was also Malaysia's best overall rider in the 2007, 2008 and 2009 editions.
"It is a steep climb rather than a wider and more gradual ascent like Cameron Highlands.
"So, just like Genting Highlands, we could see the peloton breaking apart and possibly a solo finish."

Yong Li, who has also served as an assistant sports director with Kuwait Pro Cycling Team, believes the Malaysian riders would already have been well briefed by their respective team management and coaching staff.
"I believe all the riders from Malaysia Pro Cycling (MPC), Terengganu Cycling Team (TSG) and the national squad would have received tips from their respective sports directors," said Yong Li
"They already know what needs to be done on the climbs at Gunung Jerai, Cameron Highlands in Stage Four and Genting Highlands. Most of their sports directors are former riders themselves."
During his racing career, Yong Li also represented RTS-Santic Racing Team, Azad University Cross Team, Letua Cycling Team, Meitan Hompo GDR and Proton T-Bikes Cycling Team.
The 2026 LTdL, classified as a 2.ProSeries race, begins on Sunday with Stage One from Shah Alam to Kampar.
The eight-stage race will conclude with the Muar-Putrajaya leg and cover a total distance of 1,285.5km.
e4eafa5822b7dd4d: KUALA LUMPUR: Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) peace panel head Mohagher Iqbal described Malaysia as an "honest broker" in talks between the Philippine government and the MILF.
Speaking to reporters after a one-day meeting of the Peace Implementing Panels of the Philippine Government and the MILF yesterday, Mohagher said Malaysia's contribution was deeply valued.
Philippine government officials did not hold a press conference.
"Malaysia is an honest broker, and it has shown the way that since 2001, Malaysia has been able to journey with the two parties, tackling and overcoming obstacles along the way.
"So, there is no reason why Malaysia should not continue as the facilitating country. It has delivered.
"Malaysia should continue and must continue with the peace process because both the government and the MILF especially have very high trust in the impartiality of Malaysia."
The conflict has claimed an estimated 150,000 lives since the 1970s, according to AFP.
Mohagher said Malaysia had been involved in the peace process since 2001 and expressed hope that it would continue to facilitate the talks until an exit agreement.
He said Malaysia's role had been instrumental in helping the two parties navigate obstacles throughout the peace process.
7c74b825589a0522: PETALING JAYA: Parti komponen Perikatan Nasional (PN) boleh memilih untuk bertanding menggunakan lambang PAS pada PRN Melaka, jika gabungan itu masih digantung Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan (JPPM), kata Takiyuddin Hassan.
Setiausaha Agung PN dan PAS itu berkata, partinya tiada halangan jika parti lain menggunakan logonya, tetapi Bersatu secara khusus diminta bertanding menggunakan lambang sendiri.

"Jadi, tidak semestinya parti-parti itu (parti dalam PN) menggunakan logo sendiri. Mereka boleh menggunakan logo mana-mana parti yang menunjukkan mereka ini bersatu bersama.
"Jadi, apa salahnya kalau ada satu dalam kalangan gabungan parti ini, iaitu PAS ke, parti lain juga menggunakan logo berkenaan. Tidak menjadi kesalahan dari sudut undang-undang.
