PAS yang menerajui PN melalui Naib Presidennya, Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, ialah komponen paling dominan dalam gabungan itu dengan memiliki 43 kerusi Parlimen dan 146 kerusi DUN.
9fc402160ba920ad: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Wondering what to check out on Apple TV this month? Here’s a list of what’s fresh on the streaming service.
The Last First: Winter K2 (Trailer here) — A harrowing look at summiting K2 in the winter
Release date: Friday, October 2nd

In The Last First: Winter K2, Amir Bar-Lev tells a complex, harrowing and moving story that takes an unflinching look at the industry of extreme mountain climbing and its changing culture. Focusing on a 2021 expedition, this documentary follows Icelander John Snorri Sigurjónsson and the Pakistani father-son team of Ali and Sajid Sadpara, a party of mountaineers who set out to be the first to summit K2 in the winter, when the mountain’s conditions are the cruelest. The men soon find themselves sharing the treacherous ascent with influencer climbers and their film crews, commercial expedition clients, and a Nepalese team no longer content to help Westerners achieve mountaineering glory. The Last First: Winter K2 takes us to the icy heights and unpredictable weather of K2 and reveals a surprising and layered story — one of strategy and determination, class and caste, money and power — all under life-and-death circumstances.
The Sisters Grimm (Season Two) — A magical mystery adventure packed with secrets, surprises and fairy-tale twists
Release date: Friday, October 2nd

In season two, one year after their parents’ mysterious disappearance, sisters Sabrina and Daphne Grimm continue uncovering the secrets of Ferryport Landing, where fairy tales and fairy-tale creatures are real. Along the way, they face new adventures and mysteries.
Small Prophets — A quirky comedy that will combines magical spirits and questions about love
Release date: Wednesday, October 7th

Small Prophets is a comic tale of the eccentric Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley) who, since his darling Clea disappeared seven years ago, has lived a very ordinary life. He works in a DIY store, visits his dad Brian (Sir Michael Palin) and hopes for Clea to return. One day Brian shares an old recipe involving rainwater, horse manure and more than a little alchemy. With recipe in hand, Michael sets out (albeit with some skepticism) to create homunculi — magical spirits that can predict the future — in the hope they have the answer to his burning question: “will I ever see Clea again?”

Michael gets help from his young coworker Kacey (Lauren Patel), an unlikely friendship that blossoms partly (but not wholly) through their mutual dislike of store manager Gordon (Mackenzie Crook). Their friendship adds to the frustration and intrigue of his nosy neighbors (Sophie Willan, Jon Pointing) who are obsessed with trying to find out what the hell is going on in the garden shed.
Matchbox The Movie (Trailer here) — A globe-trotting action adventure suitable for family viewing.
Release date: Friday, October 9th

Inspired by the iconic Mattel toys, “Matchbox The Movie” is an action-packed, globetrotting adventure about a group of friends since childhood who have their lives upended when undercover CIA agent Sean (John Cena), their long-absent former leader, returns to their small town and unwittingly gets them embroiled in a frantic international pursuit to save the world.
Tenzing (Trailer here) — The story of Tenzing Norgay, who was one of the first to summit Everest
Release date: Friday, October 16th

Based on true events, Tenzing chronicles the little-known story of Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok), a gifted Himalayan climber who, alongside New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston), became the first to summit Mount Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (Thinley Lhamo), Tenzing finds an ally in expedition secretary Jill Henderson (Caitríona Balfe). Together, they persuade Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) that Tenzing belongs on the British climbing team, rather than merely serving it. Where Western climbers see “Everest” as something to be conquered, Tenzing reveres “Chomolungma” as the sacred mother goddess. What follows is an ascent defined as much by the tensions between backgrounds, classes and competing ambitions as by the perils of the mountain itself. But high above the world, empire, rank and aspiration fall away, leaving two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust — and for Tenzing, the fulfillment of both a lifelong dream and a spiritual calling. Directed by award-winning filmmaker Jennifer Peedom, Tenzing is a story of greatness that refuses to be diminished — and the love that makes it possible.
Where’s Wanda? (Season Two) (Trailer here) — A darkly comic mystery that will keep you guessing until the very end!
Release date: Wednesday, October 21st

In season two, the Klatts (Heike Makatsch and Axel Stein) are back! Just as they thought their lives were finally returning to normal, their daughter, Wanda (Lea Drinda), is caught seemingly red-handed standing over a dead body. They will need to do everything in their power to prove her innocence and avoid losing her again, as their investigation to find the real murderer takes them into the criminal underbelly of their sleepy suburban town. But will their quest to protect their family get them all out of trouble, or ultimately lead them further astray? And can they find out the truth of what happened on that fateful day before it’s too late?
Nocturne — A chilling crime thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat!

The series tells the story of Jonah Lynn (Liev Schreiber), an ex-soldier turned homicide detective who, tired of working the tough streets of Philadelphia, moves to a small town in western Pennsylvania for a quiet life. But, as the town and his family come under attack from the diabolically cunning serial killer Jurek Walter (Stephen Graham), Jonah must protect all that he holds dear. When the desperate search for Jurek’s last missing victim forces Jonah to send his surrogate daughter, FBI Agent Saga Bauer (Zazie Beetz), up against Jurek, how far will Jonah go?
Binge watchable:
Ted Lasso (Season Four) (Trailer here) — A feel-good comedy about kindness, friendship and finding hope in unexpected places
Final Episode: October 7th

Ted returns to Richmond, taking on his biggest challenge yet: coaching a second division women’s football team. Throughout the course of the season, Ted and the team learn to leap before they look, taking chances they never thought they would.

Police detective Ian Ridley’s (Patrick Brammall) life fell apart 11 years ago when his young daughter, Maggie, disappeared without a trace. Now working as a police dispatcher, the only thing that has kept him going is his implacable refusal to accept that she might be gone forever. When he receives a distress call from a teenage girl he is certain is Maggie, he will stop at nothing to find her and reunite his broken family, whatever the cost.
b40287b459a789b5: KUALA LUMPUR: Veteran singer Hasnol has opened up about a difficult chapter in his life, revealing that he is currently staying in temporary workers' quarters provided by a friend in Shah Alam, Selangor.
The 56-year-old artiste, whose real name is Hasnol Hassan Ariff, said he is working hard to rebuild his life while searching for a stable income.
His financial situation has hit such a low point that he often skips meals to stretch his daily budget for essentials.
"That's just reality for me right now. I eat whatever I can afford. If all I can get is roti canai, then that's what gets me through the day," he shared.

Best known for his 90s hit Laguku Untukmu, Hasnol admitted that his current life is a far cry from his heyday. Even so, he is choosing to stay positive and accept the situation as part of his journey.
"Maybe this is a gentle reminder from God to return to Him. He can take away luxury at any moment. I've accepted what has been fated for me," he said.
To make ends meet, Hasnol drives for an e-hailing service during the week and busks on weekends. While he still gets queries for singing gigs, turning interest into actual paid work remains tricky.
"I still get invitations to perform, but people often ask about my rates and then go silent," he explained.
His current hardship follows a tough setback earlier in May, when he was forced to vacate his rented home after falling behind on payments.
At the time, he made a public appeal for work with only 10 days left to pack up and leave.
bcdd17c365b9d379: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) may contest the Melaka state election under the PAS logo if the coalition’s suspension by the Registrar of Societies (RoS) remains in force, secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said today.
According to Harian Metro, Takiyuddin said the choice of logo was not a major issue for the coalition, which would decide its approach according to the circumstances ahead of the election.
He said PAS had no difficulty contesting under its own logo, while Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia could also contest using its own symbol.

Takiyuddin added that parties in an electoral alliance did not necessarily have to use their respective logos, pointing to the 2018 general election, when DAP, PKR and Bersatu candidates contested under the PKR symbol.
“So, it is not necessary for those parties [within PN] to use their own logos. They can use the logo of any party that shows they are united together.
“So what is wrong if one of the parties in the coalition — PAS, for example — or the other parties also use that logo? There is nothing unlawful about it.
“This is among the options we have if PN remains suspended,” he was quoted as saying at the Bunut Payong Cakna Rakyat Carnival in Kota Bharu.

The RoS ordered PN to suspend all activities with effect from September 23 under subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966. The notice was issued following a complaint lodged with the department by Bersatu.
PN has also been issued a notice requiring it to explain why its registration should not be cancelled.
The Melaka state assembly was dissolved with effect from September 23, paving the way for the state election.
At the previous state election on November 20, 2021, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 seats to form the government, while Pakatan Harapan secured five and PN two.
932cfd575f5f4a68: PADANG BESAR, Sept 26 — The Communications Ministry, through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), will help the Health Ministry (MoH) provide free postal delivery of medicines to patients who opt for the service from October 1.

Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and Perlis Health director Dr Ghazali Chik.

7efb801b7ffa0ec0: PETALING JAYA: The national men’s hockey team's winning run at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games continued today as the Speedy Tigers defeated Pakistan 5-4 in their Group B tie.
Malaysia trailed 3-4 at one point before staging a comeback to snatch a win, dealing Pakistan its first defeat in the Asian Games.

fd498b953952200a: KUALA LUMPUR: The national men's hockey team fought back in the last four minutes to edge Pakistan 5-4 in an Asian Games Group B match in Gifu today, virtually qualifying for the semi-finals.
World No. 15 Malaysia now top the group with 12 points from four matches and will face China in their final group match on Monday.

91d020c9b499891f: WASHINGTON, Sept 26 — China and the United States agreed to set up a “communication channel” for artificial intelligence incidents, the White House said Friday, after a Washington summit short on breakthroughs.

Donald Trump and Xi Jinping discussed matters ranging from AI and trade to the stalled war in Iran, and confirmed that they would meet for a third and fourth time this year at international summits in China and the United States.
Xi’s visit to Washington was marked more by pomp than substance, but the White House said the nations agreed to establish a “bilateral communication channel” for AI incidents.
While billionaire Trump has repeatedly dismissed fears that AI could pose a threat to humanity, Xi took a more measured tone, noting the technology must develop under human control.
The White House also reported some deals from the visit, including China agreeing to import at least 10 million metric tonnes of coal from the US in 2027 and 2028.
Additionally, the two countries agreed more favourable tariff treatment for US$30 billion (RM126 billion) of “non-sensitive goods” in each direction and two Chinese pandas were to arrive at a US zoo.
Beijing did not immediately comment after the White House statements.

Despite the focus on pomp and ceremony during the visit, the message from the US and Chinese sides was that the summit had nevertheless helped smooth tensions between the rival superpowers over a host of issues.
Trump said the meeting was “one of Friendship, Strength, and Success, for both China and the U.S.A.”
“We’ve made great strides, very positive for both countries,” Trump told reporters as he had tea with Xi at the White House on Friday before the archives trip.
‘Strategic stability’

Trump rolled out the red carpet throughout the visit, treating Xi to a state banquet full of US tech titans, plus military parades, a flyover and even a tour of his new White House helipad and ballroom.
For his part, Xi said his Washington trip had added “new substance” to his summit with Trump in Beijing in May.
The Chinese leader added that they had agreed to “strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity.”
The announcement that the two leaders would continue their dialogue was perhaps the biggest deliverable for both sides.
Both leaders confirmed they would meet again at the APEC summit in Shenzen, China, in November and the G20 forum at Trump’s Doral resort in Miami in December.

While visiting the National Archives in Washington, the leaders inspected the Declaration of Independence, which marks its 250th anniversary this year and which set out the path for American independence from the “tyrant” British king.
Beneath the rotunda, Trump also showed Xi the US Constitution, the document that set out the principles of the country’s democratic government two and a half centuries ago.

“We’re just comparing how this goes 250 years, theirs goes 6,000 years,” Trump told reporters, referring to China’s ancient roots, as he stood alongside Xi, chairman of the Chinese Communist Party, which has ruled China since 1949.
Iran talks
Trump confirmed during the archive visit that the two leaders had discussed the US-Israeli war in Iran, which is approaching its seven-month mark.
The Republican has faced pressure from Democrats and his own party to confront Xi over reports that Beijing has supplied Tehran with intelligence for attacks on US troops.
“We did, we did,” Trump said at the National Archives when asked if they had talked about Iran.
Asked if he thought there would be progress on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which is crucial for the flow of oil, Trump replied: “I think we’re going to do great.”

Trump’s showcasing of US democracy at the National Archives comes a week after he banned three major US media outlets from the White House. They were readmitted on Thursday on the orders of a US judge.
The First Amendment of the US Constitution protects the freedom of the press.
Rights groups criticise China for its lack of press freedoms and the right of free expression.

Trump also publicly mocked his democratically elected predecessor Joe Biden as he gave Xi a tour of the White House on Thursday, showing him a picture of an “autopen” that he has mounted in a gallery of US presidents instead of Biden’s portrait. — AFP
4a666d5e31bc5f6c: NEW YORK, Sept 26 — Malaysia has stressed that pandemic prevention, preparedness and response must be treated as both a national imperative and a shared global responsibility, drawing on lessons from the Covid-19 pandemic.

“Covid-19 exposed a fundamental truth. No nation can secure its health in isolation,” said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan in Malaysia’s statement at the High-Level Meeting on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response here yesterday.
Mohamad is in New York from September 23 to 27 to lead Malaysia’s delegation to the 81st session of the UN General Assembly (UNGA).
Malaysia has translated this lesson into action, Mohamad shared at the meeting.

“Through the Malaysia National Action Plan for Health Security 2025–2030, we are strengthening health-system readiness, integrated surveillance and early warning, laboratory capacity, emergency coordination, and a prepared health workforce,” he said.
Taking public health seriously, Mohamad said Malaysia is implementing the ‘One Health’ approach to mitigate microbiological threats in food, water and the environment.
“We believe that only through a whole-of-society approach would public health be assured nationwide,” he said.
The foreign minister noted that stronger preparedness will remain incomplete without equity.

Malaysia, he said, welcomes the WHO Pandemic Agreement and “we call for a robust and equitable Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing Annex that places pathogen sharing and benefit-sharing on an equal footing, while respecting national legislation and State sovereignty.”
Mohamad said equity must also be supported by the capacity to research, develop and produce essential health products.
Through its National Vaccine Development Roadmap 2021–2030, Malaysia is strengthening these capabilities.
Looking ahead, Mohamad said Malaysia’s collective ambition must be matched by sustainable means.
“Financing should be adequate, predictable and responsive to public health risks, equity and country needs.
“International mechanisms must complement domestic investment, strengthen national capacities, and reinforce universal health coverage,” he said.

The true test of this meeting, Mohamad said, will not be the commitments we announce, but whether the next threat is detected earlier, contained faster and met with fairer access to life-saving tools.
“Let us make solidarity not an improvised response to crisis, but a standing commitment secured before the next emergency, for every nation and every generation,” he said.

The meeting was held under the theme “Fostering a Multilateral and Intergenerational Approach to Prevent, Prepare for and Respond to Pandemics and Public Health Emergencies, Through the Principles of Equity and Solidarity” at the UN Headquarters. — Bernama
c3b676512295b46d: NAGOYA: China's 17-year-old sprinter Chen Yujie said she has "no limits" after dominating the women's 100m final for Asian Games gold.
Chen stormed to victory in a Games-record 11.06sec in Nagoya to showcase her potential.
Chen, who turns 18 in December, called Friday's emphatic victory "the best present for my birthday."
But the teenager does not want to stop there.
"Now I am the champion of the Asian Games and I want to achieve more on the international stage, at the world championships and at the Olympics," she said.
"Now that I have become a champion, my goal will be to defend my title in the future.
"I am now in the position of challenging someone else, instead of waiting to be challenged by others."
Chen, who will also race in the 200m at the Games, added: "I have no limits."
Chinese media on Saturday hailed what it hopes will be a new era for Chinese sprinting, having never won 100m or 200m Olympic gold.
The official website of the Olympics proclaimed her a "new sprint star."
"I want to leave my mark for the Chinese women's sprinters and for the Asian sprinters," said Chen.
Despite the victory Chen admitted she had been nervous before the final.
"When I was on the training track my legs were shaking," said the teenager, who beat two-time Olympian Shanti Pereira of Singapore into second by 0.15sec.
"I was very scared that this could lead to a false start. I thought a lot about that."
Chen also defeated the 30-year-old Pereira to win the 200m at the 2025 Asian Athletics Championships. --AFP
4e50ff85b8980f89: NAGOYA: Japan have been "progressing steadily" near the halfway stage of the Asian Games, the host's head of mission said, but they are also drawing inspiration from behemoth China, who breached the 100-gold mark at the Aichi-Nagoya Games on Saturday.
The hosts remain on course to surpass their haul of 52 golds from the Hangzhou Games three years ago, even as China continue to set the benchmark with characteristic dominance.

"At this halfway point, we've been told by our strategy team that we are progressing steadily in terms of the number of medals, including gold medals, as well as our overall medal count," Japan's Kosei Inoue told a press conference.
"More than the medal count, what makes me really happy is that each athlete and each team set a goal of producing their best performance and then achieved it.
"We'll keep supporting them so they can reach the goals they set for these Games and perform in a way that carries them forward to the next step."
With an eye on the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, Japan aim to maximise athlete performance in the second half of the Games, including by learning directly from China's success.
"I've seen the Chinese team excel and perform brilliantly," former Olympic judo champion Inoue said.
"For team Japan, that is a big stimulus and a learning opportunity, both for these Games and for the future of sport.
"There is a lot we can learn from them. We want to keep growing and keep working hard to catch up, even if only little by little." --REUTERS
9ec47ef5d2ab850a: PARIS, Sept 26 — MotoGP has added two new circuits in Argentina and Australia to the 22-race 2027 calendar, announced on Friday.
The season is scheduled to open in Buriram, Thailand, on March 7 and end in Valencia, Spain, on November 28.

The first new track will be in Buenos Aires in April, the second leg of a three-race American swing that starts with Goiania in Brazil, which staged its first race this season, and finishes in Austin, Texas.
The second addition is a street circuit in Adelaide on November 14 at the end of a five-race late-season swing down through Asia to Australia.
The Autodromo Oscar y Juan Galvez in Buenos Aires replaces Termas de Rio Hondo, more than 1,100 kilometres inland from the capital.
That circuit was on and off the MotoGP calendar between 2014 and its last appearance in 2025. Buenos Aires last hosted races in 1999.

In Australia, Phillip Island near Melbourne has hosted races since 1989, but its contract expires after this season and the Victoria State Government rejected a plan by MotoGP to move the race to the track used by Formula One in Albert Park in the heart of the city.
The race in Adelaide, which will require laying track in parklands, has met with local opposition.
Hungary has been dropped from the schedule after just two years. The race was poorly attended and the Balaton Park circuit was reportedly unpopular with riders. — AFP

4282f364961a2ac7: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — A 16-year-old Form Four student detained in connection with the murder investigation into the death of a Form Two student at a Kuala Pilah school has been remanded for six days, until October 1.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the remand application was made at the Seremban Magistrates’ Court today.
“Police applied for the teenager to be remanded this morning and the court granted a six-day remand beginning today, until October 1,” he said to Harian Metro.
Police had earlier said the student was detained to assist investigations after the death was classified as murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
Preliminary investigations found that the incident took place at the school hostel at about 8pm on Friday.
The victim was taken to Kuala Pilah Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
Police are continuing to examine the evidence to establish the circumstances surrounding the death and any possible motive.
Alzafny had earlier urged the public not to speculate or circulate unverified information, saying this could interfere with the investigation and affect the privacy of the families involved.
The Education Ministry has ordered an immediate audit of the school and said it would cooperate fully with police.
201b08c000b53f0e: KUALA LUMPUR: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah today graced the launch of 'Kembara Dunia: 100 Hari, 40 Syarahan, 15 Negara', documenting former Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) vice-chancellor Professor Emeritus Datuk Seri Dr Zaini Ujang's intellectual journey across 15 countries.
Zaini said the 100-day journey, which took place from April 16 to July 26, 2025, covered 15 countries, including Japan, Germany and the United States.
During the journey, he delivered 40 lectures and met more than 1,000 people, including new acquaintances, with whom he exchanged views and experiences in various settings.

The former secretary-general of several ministries said his training in chemical engineering had shaped his approach to the thoughts, events and experiences he encountered during the journey, which he treated as inputs to be processed and reflected upon.

"I also had the opportunity to discuss, explore and reassess various important questions about life, particularly careers and contributions, education, development, leadership, sustainability and the future of global society," he said in his speech at the launch.
Sultan Nazrin also launched the book, published by UTM Press, at the event, which was attended by Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad.
The book brings together Zaini's experiences, observations and reflections on developments in knowledge, research and higher education, as well as the lives of communities in various countries.

UTM vice-chancellor Professor Dr Mohd Shafry Mohd Rahim said the experiences documented in the book highlighted the importance of intellectual mobility in broadening perspectives and strengthening knowledge networks across borders.

"In an increasingly interconnected world, universities need to produce scholars who are not only knowledgeable but also broad-minded, capable of engaging in dialogue across cultures and courageous enough to bring Malaysia's wealth of knowledge to the international stage," he said.
Shafry said such journeys served as a reminder that academic life was not confined to lecture halls, laboratories or campuses.
He said UTM sought to strengthen intellectual mobility through its Strategic Plan 2030.
Zaini received the Merdeka Award in 2009 and the 2025 National Engineering Figure Award.
He has also produced more than 300 scientific articles, 2,000 general articles and 58 books.
265a7a262098094f: PETALING JAYA: Pembatalan pelantikan 10 exco Negeri Sembilan sah mengikut peruntukan undang-undang negeri, kata Peguam Negara, Dusuki Mokhtar.
Menurutnya, warta pembatalan itu yang berkuat kuasa 20 Sept lalu sejajar Perkara 38(5) Undang-undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan 1959.

"Berdasarkan warta Perkara 38(5) Undang-undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan 1959, seseorang exco selain menteri besar memegang jawatannya selama diperkenan Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir," katanya menurut Sinar Harian.
Pentadbiran Negeri Sembilan mewartakan pembatalan pelantikan 10 exco Khamis lalu, dengan pemecatan mereka berkuat kuasa 20 Sept lalu.
Warta itu menyebut pelantikan mereka dibatalkan dan terbatal kerana melanggar ikrar taat setia kepada Tuanku Muhriz.

Sepuluh bekas exco itu terdiri daripada tujuh wakil Umno, iaitu Mustapha Nagoor (Palong), Faizal Ramli (Linggi), Zaiful Bahri Idris (Chembong), Razi Ali (Sungai Lui), Asna Amin (Lenggeng), Siti Nur Umaira Hasim (Labu) dan Suhaimizan Bizar (Gemencheh).
Baki tiga lagi ialah Siow Kong Choon (Chennah) daripada MCA, wakil PAS Fairuz Isa (Serting) dan Razali Abu Samah (Sikamat) daripada Wawasan.

Pemecatan itu menyusul seminggu selepas mereka mengeluarkan kenyataan didakwa mengesahkan penyingkiran Tuanku Muhriz sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar, sebelum disokong Menteri Besar, Ismail Lasim keesokannya.
Bagaimanapun, perkara itu dipertikaikan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negeri Sembilan serta Jabatan Peguam Negara.
dff5eec7e87582d0: SANDAKAN, Sept 26 — Road users are calling for urgent repairs to a badly damaged stretch of road along Batu 32 here, opposite the Road Transport Department (JPJ) checkpoint, following years of what they described as neglect.

Resident Mohd Hakimi raised concern over the condition of the road, describing it as a lifeline for the local community that had been left without comprehensive repairs despite its deteriorating state.
His concern intensified after he witnessed a vehicle stranded by the roadside after being disabled by the severely damaged road surface.
He said the incident highlighted the danger faced by motorists and other road users who depend on the route daily.
According to Mohd Hakimi, breakdowns caused by deep potholes, including blown tyres and damaged rims, had become increasingly common among residents using the road.
He said the deteriorating condition was not only a safety hazard but also placed an additional financial burden on vehicle owners, who had to bear repair and maintenance costs.
Mohd Hakimi questioned why basic infrastructure such as safe and properly maintained roads remained an unresolved issue despite the country having been independent for decades.
He also questioned the level of monitoring by the authorities, particularly as the damaged stretch is located near a JPJ enforcement facility.
He called on the local authority, Public Works Department (JKR) and road maintenance concessionaires to visit the site and see for themselves the difficulties faced by road users.
Mohd Hakimi said patchwork repairs were no longer sufficient, as such repairs often deteriorated again within a short period, particularly during the rainy season.
Instead, he called for comprehensive and quality resurfacing works to ensure the road remained durable in the long term.

He warned that apart from causing damage to vehicles, the poor road condition could also contribute to serious or fatal accidents, particularly involving motorcyclists and motorists travelling at night when visibility is reduced.

Residents are now hoping the relevant authorities and elected representatives will give serious attention to the matter and implement a permanent solution before the situation results in a serious accident or loss of life. — Daily Express
08527034acea93b5: PETALING JAYA: Perikatan Nasional component parties could opt to contest under the PAS banner in the upcoming Melaka polls if the coalition remains suspended by the Registrar of Societies, says Takiyuddin Hassan.
Takiyuddin, secretary-general of both PN and PAS, said his party had no qualms with other parties using its logo, although Bersatu specifically has been asked to contest under its own logo.
Nonetheless, he said, which logo the coalition uses in the Melaka polls is not that important, Harian Metro reported.
"It's not a must for each component to contest under its own logo. They can all use the same logo to show a united front.
"So there would be nothing wrong with one of the PN party's logos being used by all components, whether PAS's or another's.
"These are among our options if PN remains suspended (when the Melaka election nominations are held)," he said.
The Election Commission will meet on Oct 7 to set the key dates for the Melaka polls, following the dissolution of the state assembly on Wednesday.
On the same day the Melaka legislature was dissolved, the RoS suspended PN over a complaint filed by Bersatu. The coalition has been given 30 days to explain itself over the complaint.
PAS, which chairs PN through its vice-president Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, is the most dominant component in the coalition with 43 parliamentary seats and 146 state seats to its name.
057370481553a567: MANILA, Sept 26 — The Philippines temporarily suspended excise duties on petroleum products used for cooking, the presidential palace said on Friday, as it struggles to deal with soaring fuel costs from the Middle East war.
The temporary suspension covers liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), the country’s main fuel for cooking, as well as kerosene, according to an executive order released to the media on Friday.

“The excise taxes on LPG, except when used as a raw material for production of petrochemical products or used for motive power, and kerosene, except when used as aviation fuel, are hereby fully suspended,” it said.
The cut translates to a reduction of about three pesos (about five US cents) per kilogramme of LPG.
The excise cut followed a threat by bus operators to hold a two-day nationwide transport strike next week to press the government to let them raise fares, which are state-regulated.
Fuel prices in the Philippines are unregulated, unlike neighbours including Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, leaving local transport firms to deal with market fluctuations.
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr said the tax would automatically revert after three months, or a week after the one-month average Dubai crude oil price falls below US$80 (RM336) per barrel.
He said the average crude oil price over the 30 days to September 11 had reached US$99.41 (RM418.02).
The import-dependent Philippines declared a national energy emergency in March and has been forced to cast an ever-wider net for fuel, including purchases of oil from Russia.
The war in the Middle East and high inflation trimmed the Philippines’ economic growth in the first half to 2.6 per cent, well below government targets. — AFP
e06a024ea9a91382: The French president’s resolve seems to have rubbed off on the leaders of other ‘middle powers’ On the first day of the United Nations general assembly this week, two world leaders outlined competing visions for the future. Donald Trump’s speech was disturbingly familiar to those he’s given before: a litany of false boasts and odd tangents, peppered with grim military threats against a variety of nation states. Discussing his seven-month war with Iran, he mused over whether to “annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly”. In Trump’s eyes, the world is there to be ruled – and ruled only by the US, whose economy is “the envy of the world” and military is “the most powerful on Earth”. Steve Bloomfield is the former international editor of the Observer Continue reading...
6b484bc254ddce65: Trump tries to dominate at the UN as his approval ratings plummet and even some Republicans stray from the script Donald Trump stood before the United Nations on Tuesday and threatened to “annihilate” Iran. Yet even as the most powerful man on the planet flexed his military muscles, he was powerless to keep the gravitational pull of domestic politics at bay. Heading into the UN building in New York, the US president was questioned by Kaitlan Collins, an anchor at CNN, which he had banned from the White House before a judge ruled against him. “I’m surprised that CNN is here covering me,” the 80-year-old snapped. “You should not be here covering me.” Continue reading...
a378f01f67018095: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) has allocated RM28.12 million for phased maintenance and upgrading works at the Batu Muda People’s Housing Programme (PPR) here.

Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the allocation to improve various facilities at the housing scheme was expected to benefit more than 10,000 residents, provided they took good care of the facilities.

“As long as Malaysians do not know how to maintain cleanliness, money will continue to be spent on cleaning operations, and we will not have enough funds for development,” she told reporters during the Mega Cleaning Programme in conjunction with Malaysia Clean-Up Day and a walkabout to inspect maintenance works at PPR Batu Muda today.
She stressed that maintaining cleanliness through the Malaysia Clean-Up initiative should become a continuous habit rather than merely a one-off programme.
The programme was also attended by Batu MP P. Prabakaran and Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud.

Meanwhile, DBKL said in a statement that upgrading works completed at PPR Batu Muda included the replacement of 21 lifts costing RM11.69 million, which was completed in October last year and is currently within the Defects Liability Period (DLP).
DBKL also completed road resurfacing works costing RM1.46 million, as well as the upgrading of a children’s playground at the housing scheme at a cost of RM278,000. — Bernama
3c64b5eaedc2fede: MANILA, Sept 26 — A Filipina who spent almost 15 years on death row in Indonesia for drug trafficking walked free on Friday after receiving a presidential pardon.
A beaming Mary Jane Veloso clutched the document signed by President Ferdinand Marcos granting her “absolute pardon” after leaving her Manila prison cell late on Friday.
“I wish to convey my gratitude to our dear president who cleared my name and allowed me to reunite with my family,” she told a news conference.
Veloso said she was looking forward to being reunited with her two sons.
“I was unable to supervise them as they grew up, but I believe it’s not too late,” she said.
Veloso was arrested and sentenced to death by an Indonesian court in 2010 after the suitcase she was carrying was found to be lined with 2.6 kilograms (5.7 pounds) of heroin.

Indonesia spared her from execution in 2015 after Philippines authorities arrested her suspected recruiter, who is accused of duping her into carrying the false-bottomed suitcase containing the illegal drugs.
Jakarta handed her over to Manila in 2024 under a “practical arrangement” for her repatriation, allowing her to serve the rest of her sentence in a Philippine prison.
“I’ll give you a scoop: I signed her pardon yesterday,” Marcos told reporters earlier on Friday.
Veloso had travelled to Indonesia to seek work as a maid and her case sparked uproar in the Philippines.

Many Filipinos regarded her as a poster child of the Philippine economic diaspora — the millions of able-bodied Filipinos who seek better-paying work abroad in hopes of helping their families escape widespread poverty.
She and her supporters maintained she was duped by an international drug syndicate.
“They were so happy,” her mother, Celia Veloso, said earlier of Veloso’s two sons after being informed of the pardon.
“‘We will finally be able to be with mama’, that’s what they told me,” she told AFP by phone. — AFP
eb09dc1e95c83544: PETALING JAYA: Physical bullying topped the list of complaints received by the anti-bullying tribunal, making up 41 of the total 56 cases reported as of yesterday.
Tribunal president Nurul Husna Awang said these cases involved students allegedly being beaten, pushed, kicked or having their belongings damaged, Berita Harian reported.
She added that the tribunal also received six complaints of emotional and psychological bullying in the form of threats, insults or actions that caused victims to be fearful, shameful or stressed.
The tribunal formed in June also received five complaints of verbal bullying, three related to cyber bullying and one of "social bullying".
She added that teens aged 13 to 17 made up the majority of victims with 35 cases, while 18 cases involved children aged seven to 12, and three involved children aged below seven.
"In terms of ethnicity, 29 victims are Chinese, 24 Malay and three from Indian households," she said. adding that 33 of the 56 victims are boys.
"There are also 86 respondents in these 56 cases, involving 65 boys and 21 girls, meaning in some cases there is more than one perpetrator."

According to Nurul, 12 cases are active while 44 have been resolved, including 37 which were rejected at the vetting stage, six that were resolved following hearings, and one that was withdrawn by the complainant.

Law and institutional reform minister Azalina Othman Said previously said five cases were decided through various awards, including bullies being made to apologise to their victims, undergo counselling or, in one case, pay RM2,000 in damages.

The tribunal serves as a second avenue for victims who believe their complaints are not properly addressed by educational institutions. It also handles cases involving children outside the school system.

Yesterday, a Form 2 student at a sports school in Kuala Pilah, Negeri Sembilan, died after allegedly being beaten up by a senior. A 16-year-old student has since been arrested to assist in the murder investigation.
89d72adbebbac173: PETALING JAYA: Penganalisis politik Ong Kian Ming meramalkan Pengerusi Barisan Nasional (BN), Zahid Hamidi akan menjadi perdana menteri jika BN dan Perikatan Nasional (PN) membentuk pakatan serta memenangi PRU16.

Bekas pemimpin DAP itu berkata, PAS mungkin memenangi lebih banyak kerusi berbanding BN, tetapi beliau menjangkakan Zahid akan mendapat sokongan parti dari Sabah dan Sarawak untuk jawatan tertinggi itu.
"Saya rasa naratif penyatuan ummah dan penyatuan Melayu-Islam ini adalah satu naratif yang akan membolehkan gelombang biru menjadi satu realiti pada PRU16.
"BN dan PN akan memenangi lebih daripada 112 kerusi Parlimen di Semenanjung dan mereka akan membentuk kerajaan bersama Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) dan Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS).
"Pada masa sama, Zahid akan menjadi perdana menteri ke-11," katanya menurut Sinar Harian.

Bekas Ahli Parlimen itu mengimbas peristiwa Naib Presiden Umno ketika itu, Ismail Sabri Yaakob, dilantik perdana menteri pada Ogos 2021 dan bagaimana timbul isu hierarki kepimpinan di mana "presiden Umno boleh 'overrule' perdana menteri".
Disebabkan kecenderungan untuk mengelakkan isu sedemikian berulang, beliau berkata, Zahid mempunyai peluang lebih cerah untuk menjadi perdana menteri berbanding pemimpin Umno lain.
Ong turut meramalkan Pakatan Harapan (PH) akan kembali ke blok pembangkang, dengan hanya mampu mempertahankan kira-kira 40 hingga 50 kerusi Parlimen.
"Bahkan kerajaan Selangor yang dipegang PH sejak 2008 pun mungkin jatuh."
PH kini memiliki 76 kerusi Parlimen.
Umno mungkin tak pertahan semua 21 kerusi di Melaka
Ong turut meramalkan BN tidak akan bertanding di semua 21 kerusi dimenanginya pada PRN Melaka lalu, walaupun sebelum ini ia menyuarakan hasrat untuk mempertahankan kerusi terbabit.

Sebaliknya, beliau menjangkakan BN akan menyerahkan sekurang-kurangnya empat kerusi kepada PN sebagai pertukaran bagi beberapa kerusi yang kini dipegang PAS di kubu kuat parti itu di Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan dan Terengganu.
"Namun, antara kekangan terbesar ialah jika berlaku ketidaksefahaman dalam pengagihan kerusi, termasuk sekiranya PN mahukan lebih banyak kerusi, tetapi BN tidak bersetuju."
Beliau juga tidak menjangkakan BN akan mendapat sokongan mencukupi untuk mendesak PRU16 diadakan ketika ini, walaupun mungkin ada perkembangan baharu selepas pembentangan Belanjawan 2027 bulan depan.
"Pada masa itu, GPS dan GRS mungkin lebih terbuka menerima tawaran kerjasama daripada BN.
"Sekiranya senario itu berlaku dan sokongan terhadap kerajaan perpaduan berubah, ia boleh membawa kepada pembubaran Parlimen dan PRU16."
BN mendesak Perdana Menteri, Anwar Ibrahim mengadakan PRU16 lebih awal, khasnya selepas hubungan dengan PH menjadi keruh susulan pertembungan dalam PRN Johor dan Negeri Sembilan.
PN, yang membantu BN mendapat majoriti dua pertiga di DUN Negeri Sembilan pada PRN 1 Ogos lalu, turut menyokong desakan untuk mengadakan PRU mengejut.
Tetapi, Anwar menolaknya dengan menegaskan kerajaan kekal stabil dan keutamaan segera ialah meningkatkan kesejahteraan rakyat serta menguruskan ekonomi.
69d1934846d3dbd2: NEW YORK, Sept 26 — Malaysia fully supports the establishment of a sustainable, institutional and operational mechanism, including a dedicated media platform, to document and expose Israel’s violations against the Holy Sites and worshippers in Jerusalem, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
He said Israel must be held accountable for its crimes and that its gross violations must not be ignored or normalised through repetition.

Mohamad said this in his intervention at the Joint Ministerial Meeting between the League of Arab States and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) on Jerusalem at the United Nations headquarters here yesterday.
He said Malaysia continued to hold the view that Jerusalem must remain at the very heart of the Ummah’s collective struggle and action.

As reaffirmed in the Amman Ministerial Statement of Aug 5, he said East Jerusalem was an integral part of the Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT) and the capital of the State of Palestine, consistent with the International Court of Justice’s (ICJ) Advisory Opinion of July 19, 2024.
“Importantly, the same Advisory Opinion reaffirms the illegality of Israel’s occupation of the OPT including East Jerusalem,” he said.
Mohamad stressed that Israel had no sovereignty over East Jerusalem.
“Any attempt to alter its Arab, Islamic and Christian identity or its legal and demographic character was unlawful and must be unequivocally rejected,” he stressed further.

Malaysia strongly condemned the escalating violations at Al-Aqsa Mosque/Al-Haram Al-Sharif, including repeated incursions by extremist settlers and Israeli officials, restrictions on worshippers and persistent attempts to alter the historic and legal status quo.
“These provocations risk igniting a wider religious conflict with grave consequences for regional and international peace and security,” he said.

Malaysia, Mohamad said, reaffirmed its unwavering support for the historical Hashemite Custodianship over the Islamic and Christian Holy Sites in Jerusalem, as well as all efforts to protect the rights, resilience and presence of the Palestinian people in their city.

The foreign minister said the Holy City of Jerusalem (Al-Quds Al-Sharif) could not be truly protected through mere statements of concern or expressions of condemnation, but required “sustained coordination, collective resolve and decisive action.”
Mohamad said the time has come for “our collective voice to be matched by collective action.”

“We must therefore use all necessary means to fight and end the crimes committed by Israel on Palestinians. While we continue to demand decisive actions by the UN Security Council, we can and must also take our own actions, individually and as a group.

“We commend those that have suspended bilateral, trade and social relations with Israel, and welcome sanctions imposed on certain extremist Israeli Ministers, which should be extended to other Israeli leaders who incite hatred, dehumanise Palestinians and provoke violence.”
Malaysia, Mohamad said, reiterates “our call on all Member States to halt the provision of arms and financial support to Israel, so as not to become complicit in its illegal war and occupation.”
“Once again, Malaysia reiterates its unwavering commitment to defending the Holy City of Jerusalem (Al-Quds Al-Sharif) and the Palestinian cause.

“We reaffirm our solidarity with the Palestinian people and our steadfast support for their right to self-determination and the realisation of an independent State of Palestine based on the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.”
Mohamad is in New York from September 23 to 27 to lead Malaysia’s delegation to the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA). — Bernama
b538bf965f6c3802: PETALING JAYA: The revocation of the appointments of 10 Negeri Sembilan executive council members is valid, says Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar.
Dusuki said the gazette on the revocation, effective Sept 20, aligns with Article 38(5) of the state's constitution, Sinar Harian reported.
"According to Article 38(5), an exco member other than the menteri besar holds the post at the pleasure of the Yang Dipertuan Besar," he said.
The Negeri Sembilan administration gazetted the revocation of the 10 exco members' appointments on Thursday, with their sackings effective Sept 20.
The gazette said their appointments were revoked and annulled as they had violated their pledge of allegiance to the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

The 10 now-former exco members include Umno’s Mustapha Nagoor (Palong), Faizal Ramli (Linggi), Zaiful Bahri Idris (Chembong), Razi Ali (Sungai Lui), Asna Amin (Lenggeng), Siti Nur Umaira Hasim (Labu) and Suhaimizan Bizar (Gemencheh).
The other three are MCA’s Siow Kong Choon (Chennah), PAS’s Fairuz Isa (Serting) and Razali Abu Samah (Sikamat) of Wawasan.
Their sackings come a week after they issued a statement purportedly affirming Tuanku Muhriz’s removal as Yang Dipertuan Besar. Menteri besar Ismail Lasim endorsed the statement a day later.
This was disputed by the state’s Dewan Keadilan dan Undang as well as the Attorney-General’s Chambers.
fd440161623887f9: NAGOYA: China's 17-year-old sprinter Chen Yujie said she has "no limits" after dominating the women's 100m final for Asian Games gold.
Chen stormed to victory in a Games-record 11.06sec in Nagoya to showcase her potential.
Chen, who turns 18 in December, called Friday's emphatic victory "the best present for my birthday".
But the teenager does not want to stop there.
"Now I am the champion of the Asian Games and I want to achieve more on the international stage, at the world championships and at the Olympics," she said.
"Now that I have become a champion, my goal will be to defend my title in the future.
"I am now in the position of challenging someone else, instead of waiting to be challenged by others."
Chen, who will also race in the 200m at the Games, added: "I have no limits."
Chinese media on Saturday hailed what it hopes will be a new era for Chinese sprinting, having never won 100m or 200m Olympic gold.
The official website of the Olympics proclaimed her a "new sprint star".
"I want to leave my mark for the Chinese women's sprinters and for the Asian sprinters," said Chen.
Despite the victory Chen admitted she had been nervous before the final.
"When I was on the training track my legs were shaking," said the teenager, who beat two-time Olympian Shanti Pereira of Singapore into second by 0.15sec.
"I was very scared that this could lead to a false start. I thought a lot about that."
Chen also defeated the 30-year-old Pereira to win the 200m at the 2025 Asian Athletics Championships.
7aaa9100557699f0: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — The Serian District Police Headquarters (IPD) in Sarawak recorded an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 151 as of 9am today.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, 63 other areas nationwide logged moderate readings.
They included Sri Aman, Sarawak (98); Batu Pahat, Johor (81); Cheras, Kuala Lumpur (69); Klang, Selangor (62); and Kimanis, Sabah (56).
Only three areas recorded good air quality: Tanah Merah, Kelantan (47); Langkawi, Kedah (46); and Besut, Terengganu (43).
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and anything above 300 hazardous. — Bernama
5e52a8586057a118: PETALING JAYA: Political analyst Ong Kian Ming predicts that Barisan Nasional chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi will become the next prime minister should BN and Perikatan Nasional form a pact and win the next general election (GE16).
The former DAP leader said PAS was likely to win more seats than BN, but he expected Zahid to have the backing of Sabah and Sarawak parties for the top post, Sinar Harian reported.
"I feel that the narrative of a Malay-Muslim unity will enable the 'blue wave' (of a BN and PN alliance) to win GE16.
"BN and PN will win more than 112 parliamentary seats in Peninsular Malaysia, and they will form a coalition government with Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) and Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS).
"And Zahid will become the 11th prime minister," Ong was quoted as saying.

The former DAP MP recalled when then Umno vice-president Ismail Sabri Yaakob was appointed prime minister in August 2021, leadership hierarchy issues arose where "an Umno president overruled a prime minister".
Because of the inclination to prevent such issues from recurring, he said Zahid would have a better chance of becoming prime minister than any other Umno leader.
Ong also predicted that Pakatan Harapan will return to the opposition bench, with the coalition retaining around 40 to 50 parliamentary seats.
"Even the Selangor government held by PH since 2008 might collapse," he added.
PH currently has 76 parliamentary seats.
Umno might not defend all 21 seats in Melaka
Ong also predicted that BN will not contest all 21 seats it won in the last Melaka state election, despite previously stating its intention to defend those seats.
He instead expected BN to hand about four seats to PN in exchange for several PAS-held seats in the Islamic party's strongholds of Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan and Terengganu.
"But a major hurdle might arise if both parties cannot come to an agreement on the allocation of seats. For example, if PN wants more seats and BN refuses," he said.
Ong also does not expect BN to have enough support to force GE16 to be called yet, although there could be other developments after the 2027 budget is tabled next month.
"By then, GPS and GRS might be more open to (supporting) BN (to withdraw support for the government).
"If such a scenario occurs, it could lead to the dissolution of Parliament and GE16 being called."
BN has been pushing Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim to call for an earlier GE16, especially after ties with PH soured following clashes in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections.
PN, which helped BN secure a two-thirds majority in the Negeri Sembilan assembly in the Aug 1 polls, has also backed calls for a snap general election.
However, Anwar has shot down the idea, saying the government remains stable and its immediate priority is to improve the people’s wellbeing and manage the economy.
f7cd77659da268ea: NAGOYA: Japan's 11-year-old eSports prodigy Yuki Kurihara won Asian Games gold on Saturday in style after thrashing a series of opponents up to three times his age.
The bespectacled primary school student, believed to be the youngest competitor at the Games in Aichi-Nagoya, won the Puyo Puyo Champions final 10-2.
He is host country Japan's youngest athlete in Asian Games history.
Puyo Puyo Champions is a puzzle game where players try to clear their screen of coloured blobs by lining them up and popping them.
Look unruffled throughout, Kurihara waltzed into the gold-medal match with a series of dazzling displays.
He crushed Thailand's Tanarak Wongkitkun - a relative veteran at 28 - 10-1 in the semi-finals to ensure at least a silver medal.
In the final he barely raised a smile after he beat South Korea's 24-year-old Kang Dongshin, having gone down 1-0 early on.
Kurihara started playing Puyo Puyo in his first year of primary school and soon started competing and winning in tournaments.
He obtained his pro licence in April this year and regularly beats adults.
"It's hard having to balance it with school and cram school, but it's really fun," he said ahead of the Games.
"It's the summer holidays now so I have a lot of time to practise. I want to practise a lot and develop some new strengths."
There are no publically available records of youngest medallists in the history of the Asian Games, which were first contested in 1951.
But Indonesia's Bunga Nyimas won bronze in women's skateboarding aged 12 in Jakarta in 2018.
Cui Chenxi, 13, won Games gold when she triumphed in the women's street skateboarding event three years ago in Hangzhou.

5dc380fe9b708b87: BANGKOK: Bangkok authorities declared on Saturday a disaster across all 50 districts of the Thai capital after continuous rain caused heavy flooding.
The designation, which gives local organisations authority to take action, came after the governor said almost 300mm of rain had fallen since Thursday.
"The water keeps coming in. It's hard to go out now. It's like my waist level now," said Somkid Pheuk-ngam, 67, a vendor who lives near a canal just north of central Bangkok.
"I cannot go anywhere. I have been closing my shop for two days now," she told AFP, adding that while she often gets flooded: "I think this time is worse than the 2011 flood."
The rain has fallen almost continually since Thursday afternoon, flooding roads and swelling Bangkok's canals, sending water into many homes and restaurants alongside them, AFP reporters saw.
Bangkok governor Chadchart Sittipunt said the east of the city was most impacted and warned more rain was forecast.
"The rain keeps falling and we are doing our best. We are trying to pump the water out, but the water in canals are full," he said on social media.
"The risk areas are those who live near canals. Every canal is now filled," he said, urging residents to move their cars to higher ground.
He also urged bedridden patients depending on life-saving medical equipment to consider a temporary stay in hospital.
Widespread flooding across Thailand in 2011 killed more than 500 people and damaged millions of homes.

44f6c08d92dbcc7d: Even Jacob Rees-Mogg pushes back on defining Englishness in exclusively ethnic terms. But the endurance of this discourse is still deeply troubling Can you be English and non-white? It’s a question that keeps stubbornly resurfacing in our political discourse. Last weekend, the former prime minister Rishi Sunak gave his view in a column in the Times, arguing that national identity should not be turned into a DNA test. After leaving office, Sunak, the UK’s first prime minister of colour, was subject to claims by a prominent podcaster that he was not English because he was a “brown-skinned Hindu”. Reflecting on this, Sunak described it as a “reverse Tebbit test”: the sociological concept measuring the loyalty of immigrants – and their children – in the UK depending on which cricket team they supported in international matches. “Once we say that this or that person isn’t really English or British because they are not white,” he wrote, “then we are on a very slippery slope. Some people will argue that English is an ethnic identity and British a civic identity. Though if you think those nuances are heard by most people, I fear you are being rather – perhaps even wilfully – naive.” Jason Okundaye is an assistant Opinion editor at the Guardian Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? 1e588486cc3e4e18: A tired, simplistic narrative dominates Malaysian campaign stages and social media feeds: that Malay disunity is entirely DAP's fault.

While this rhetoric is highly effective at mobilising voters through fear, it is built on a shallow foundation. Blaming DAP is a convenient distraction, one that deliberately obscures the true root causes of the Malay political crisis.

The reality is that polarisation within the Malay community is not driven by an external threat. It is the direct result of internal dynamics, clashing egos and socioeconomic evolution. DAP did not fracture Malay politics; it has merely been weaponised as a bogeyman whenever the community's internal consensus begins to splinter.

Historically, every major rupture within the Malay political establishment has originated from internal power struggles, not external interference. The historic 1987 Umno crisis — a fierce showdown between Dr Mahathir Mohamad and Tengku Razaleigh Hamzah — birthed Semangat 46.
The 1998 Reformasi movement, sparked by Anwar Ibrahim's sacking from government, led to the creation of PKR. Decades later, the 1MDB scandal triggered the 2016 split that formed Bersatu.

All of these political earthquakes occurred deep within Umno's own backyard. They were driven by leadership conflicts and raw ambition, long before DAP was ever accepted into mainstream ruling coalitions.

Furthermore, the Malay electorate is not, and has never been, a monolith. Even before independence, Malay political thought was fractured into distinct ideological factions. Malay nationalism, anchored by Umno, focused on ethnic privileges and the social contract.
Conversely, Islamic politics, championed by PAS, demanded a state rooted in religious law — a doctrinal divergence that triggered their split from Umno as early as 1951.

Today, progressive movements like PKR and Amanah contest this space by championing institutional reform and social justice within a pluralistic framework, alongside a constantly shifting constellation of splinter parties.

With segments of the electorate prioritising economic integrity, others focusing on religious identity, and some remaining loyal to traditional structures, a fragmented political landscape is inevitable.
Where, then, does DAP fit into this theatre?

The party has become a convenient rhetorical shield. When multiple Malay-based parties are forced to fish from the exact same voter pool, they inevitably fall into a hyper-nationalistic contest to prove who is "more Malay" or "more Islamic".

In this arena, the fastest way to destroy an opponent’s credibility is to label them a "puppet" or "agent" of DAP. This strategy shifts the focus away from a party's own policy failures by exploiting historical trauma and racial anxieties for short-term electoral gain.
Ultimately, a diversification of political choices is a hallmark of a maturing democracy, not a crisis to be feared. It is time for Malay political leaders to stop pointing fingers outwardly.

Blaming DAP will not reunite the community. The real challenge lies in the leadership’s inability to forge a consensus, manage ideological differences with maturity, and prioritise national stability over personal agendas.
Until they look in the mirror, they will continue fighting external shadows.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.

92373c2d48160be1: In late August, US Treasury secretary Scott Bessent declared an “economic D-Day” against Iran, promising “the single greatest financial offensive ever marshaled against an adversary”.
The D-Day analogy is an odd one for a campaign whose success ultimately depends on China, an American ally at Normandy but a strategic rival today.

For the Trump administration’s “zero-leakage” policy to succeed, foreign financial institutions would need to monitor and police their own customers. And there is no way to achieve the “total isolation” of the Iranian regime without Chinese banks doing much of the hard work of sanctions enforcement.

Before the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the US Treasury estimated that China purchased roughly 90% of Iran’s oil exports. Years of sanctions have already pushed much of the Iranian oil trade into an alternative system capable of operating without the dollar, the SWIFT interbank payments platform, and the correspondent banks that have long given the US its financial leverage.

Much of this trade moves through Iran’s rahbar shadow-banking system, which according to the Treasury processes “tens of billions of dollars” worth of trade each year, “much of it derived from Iran’s overseas sales of oil and petrochemicals”. Today, Iran settles those sales primarily in renminbi.

Secondary US sanctions have previously changed the behaviour of major Chinese banks even when China officially rejected them. Within the first week of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, for example, the offshore units of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) stopped issuing dollar-denominated letters of credit for purchases of physical Russian commodities.

Renminbi-denominated credit lines remained available for some customers but required senior management approval. The Bank of China (BOC) restricted financing for Russian commodities, while its Singapore branch went even further and ceased financing transactions involving Russian companies and oil.
America’s sanctions blind spot

But China’s largest banks—its policy banks and the “big four” state-owned commercial banks, the ICBC, the BOC, the China Construction Bank, and the Agricultural Bank of China—are not America’s hardest enforcement problem.
Their global operations require them to maintain access to dollar liquidity and correspondent banking relationships, which are far more valuable than any business with sanctioned Iranian entities.

This dependence on the global dollar system gives them powerful incentives to limit their exposure to US sanctions. As former Treasury secretary Janet L Yellen observed, China’s large banks “are not banks that we most need to worry about” as they “really, really value their correspondent-banking relations”.

The greater challenge lies deeper within the Chinese financial system, among thousands of smaller regional banks with far less exposure to the dollar-based system and therefore with less to lose if that access is cut off.
In 2023, the People’s Bank of China counted more than 3,800 urban and rural banks and credit cooperatives, in addition to private banks and other institutions.
In 2024, as the US threatened Chinese banks with secondary sanctions, Russian companies increasingly turned to smaller regional institutions with minimal ties to Western markets.

The real question facing the Trump administration is whether it can compel or induce smaller Chinese banks to scrutinise customers and transactions deliberately structured to conceal Iranian connections—and refuse the business once they uncover them.

Iran’s rahbars use foreign-exchange houses, layers of offshore shell companies, and bank accounts in the United Arab Emirates, Hong Kong, and Singapore to move oil proceeds on behalf of sanctioned Iranian entities.
Chinese buyers of Iranian crude, especially independent “teapot” refiners in Shandong, which have absorbed most of the sanctioned oil, do not need to send money to an Iranian bank.
A buyer can simply pay an offshore front company in renminbi. The money can then be used to pay Chinese suppliers on Iran’s behalf or sent elsewhere.
On paper, the transaction may have no connection to Iran. To the Chinese bank processing the payment, it could look like an ordinary transfer from a Hong Kong trading firm to a company in Dubai.

Internal records from the Iranian exchange house Radin, for example, identified dozens of China-based front companies maintaining accounts at Chinese banks. FinCEN has similarly documented transactions operated by Hong Kong-based shell companies that it linked to Iran’s shadow-banking network.

This makes compliance much harder. Instead of simply refusing to do business with sanctioned entities, banks now have to uncover hidden links to Iran in accounts and transactions where no Iranian name appears at all. That requires more than routine customer onboarding and sanctions-list screening.

Banks must scrutinise beneficial ownership and counterparties more closely and examine the purpose of payments, while anti-money laundering teams must devote resources to reviewing transaction documentation and looking for payment patterns indicating that seemingly ordinary transactions may actually be moving money for sanctioned Iranian entities.

The US Treasury is now explicitly pushing this investigative burden onto foreign banks. In April, the Office of Foreign Assets Control urged financial institutions to subject independent teapot oil refineries in China to enhanced due diligence and warned that the US government is prepared to use secondary sanctions against them.
The Treasury has since made clear that its latest sanctions campaign, Operation Economic Outcast, could include cutting foreign banks off from the dollar-based system.
The compliance trap

In principle, Chinese law already requires banks to conduct “know your customer” verification and maintain financial-crime controls. In 2022, the Financial Action Task Force rated China’s anti-money laundering regime as “largely compliant” with its due-diligence standards.

China has implemented additional measures since then. Its revised anti-money laundering law, which took effect in January 2025, requires financial institutions to verify customers and beneficial owners, understand the nature of business relationships, and, in certain high-risk cases, investigate the source of funds and the purpose of transactions.

Banks must also monitor customers and transactions and investigate activity that departs from established patterns. More detailed rules implemented in January 2026 allow banks to refuse transactions or terminate relationships when they cannot adequately resolve money-laundering concerns.

But anti-money laundering compliance and US sanctions enforcement are not the same thing. Finding an Iranian connection may prompt a Chinese bank to look more closely at a transaction if there are signs of money laundering. It does not, however, mean that under Chinese law they must reject it just because the US has sanctioned one of the parties.

In some cases, Chinese regulations pull banks in the opposite direction. In May, the Chinese ministry of commerce (Mofcom) issued a blocking order covering five independent Chinese refiners sanctioned by the US for purchasing Iranian oil. Four are smaller regional teapot refiners.

The fifth, Hengli Petrochemical’s Dalian refinery, can process 400,000 barrels a day and belongs to the Hengli Group, a Fortune 500 company. It is the largest Chinese refiner sanctioned by the US so far.

Mofcom’s order states that US sanctions against these five refiners “must not be recognised, implemented, or complied with”. Violations of the order can result in administrative penalties and expose banks and other companies to claims for damages in Chinese courts.

A Chinese bank can still refuse to process a transaction because of money-laundering concerns or other compliance risks, but it cannot refuse a transaction or sever a relationship specifically to comply with the covered US sanctions without violating the order.
As the US extends secondary sanctions to cover more economically and politically significant Chinese entities, such blocking orders are likely to become more common.
China now has a sophisticated legal and administrative apparatus that can make the extraterritorial application of US sanctions increasingly difficult—or, in some cases, moot.

This exposes a structural constraint on US sanctions power. Large state-owned Chinese banks have too much to lose if they are cut off from the dollar system. But US leverage weakens as transactions move to smaller banks with fewer ties to the US and Western financial markets.

The US government is thus left in the awkward position of asking Chinese banks to uncover hidden ties to sanctioned entities in Iran (or North Korea and Russia) and then act on those findings, even when that could put them at odds with Chinese law.

Chinese banks are certainly willing to carry out the anti-money laundering checks required by Chinese regulations, but they have little incentive to go looking for links to sanctioned entities when discovering them could create new legal problems.

In such circumstances, knowing less and maintaining plausible deniability is institutionally safer than knowing more. And unless Chinese banks closely police their own clients as payment networks adapt, sanctions will remain porous, with payments migrating to new shell companies and intermediaries.
China’s new bargaining chip

Despite having the tools to retaliate against new US sanctions, China has used them selectively. Since President Donald Trump restored “maximum pressure” on Iran in February 2025, US sanctions against Chinese entities have mostly targeted specific shadow-fleet vessels, independent refineries in Shandong Province, and shipping terminal operators (Hengli Petrochemical’s Dalian refinery, the only large integrated Chinese independent refiner sanctioned so far, remains the notable exception).
China’s response has consisted mostly of formulaic foreign ministry statements rejecting the unilateral nature of US sanctions and pledging to protect Chinese companies and citizens.

Mofcom’s May 2 blocking order remains the only consequential countermeasure, and it is narrow and targeted. Yet only days after it was issued, Chinese financial regulators reportedly instructed major Chinese banks to suspend new renminbi lending to the five sanctioned refiners while leaving existing credit lines in place.
These actions are not necessarily contradictory. China can reject the extraterritorial application of US sanctions while allowing major Chinese banks to protect themselves from the consequences.
It has followed the same pattern since Operation Economic Outcast expanded secondary sanctions in August, criticising the measures without imposing another Iran-related countermeasure.

The calculation could change if the US sanctioned a major Chinese bank or state-owned enterprise rather than another shell company, small bank, or teapot refiner. China’s largest financial institutions depend heavily on access to dollars.
The US has far less leverage over smaller and less systemically important firms. This asymmetry makes an escalating spiral of US sanctions and Chinese countermeasures less likely.

The problem for the Trump administration is what happens as more transactions move beyond the institutions and payment channels most exposed to US pressure. At that point, effective enforcement increasingly requires cooperation from Chinese banks over which the US government has no authority.
A growing renminbi-based financial system does not make US sanctions ineffective, at least while major Chinese banks remain dependent on the global dollar-based system.

But when non-dollar payments are routed through shadow intermediaries, they erode the two critical enforcement advantages on which US financial sanctions have traditionally relied: the visibility of transactions and leverage over the institutions that process them.

While the dollar system gives the US enormous financial power, American officials can no longer assume that the threat of being excluded from it will be enough to make foreign institutions comply with their dictates.
As more of the actual enforcement takes place inside China’s domestic financial system, beyond the reach of American authorities, China may gain a new source of geopolitical leverage.
Expecting China to enforce US sanctions is unrealistic, but anti-money laundering enforcement offers a more practical basis for cooperation.

As US and Chinese officials discussed Iran and its financial ties to China ahead of Trump’s planned summit with Chinese president Xi Jinping in Washington, the US would have better luck pressing China to enforce its own anti-money laundering rules against the opaque financial networks facilitating Iranian trade.

Zongyuan Zoe Liu, senior fellow for China studies at the Council on Foreign Relations, is adjunct professor of international and public affairs at Columbia University’s School of International and Public Affairs.
